evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The direction faced in prayer [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); Prayers made toward the temple (or toward the land, city and house when in exile) are heard in heaven (weight 6.0). Pair score 12.0.

Only in Solomon's blessing and dedication prayer on the bronze platform: Prayer lists famine, pestilence, blight, mildew, locust, siege and sickness as occasions for prayer; The king kneels on a bronze platform in the court and spreads his hands to heaven; An oath sworn before God's altar in the temple, judged by God; People away from Jerusalem or in exile pray in the direction of the land, city and temple; Captives confess in exile 'We have sinned, done wrong and acted wickedly'; 'Arise, YHWH, to your resting place, you and the ark of your might'; A foreigner from a far land who hears of God's name comes to pray at the temple and is heard; 'There is no man who does not sin'; Temple called a 'house of zebul' (exalted dwelling), a place for God to dwell forever; 'O my servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of God's mercy; God forgives all sins'; Heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain God, much less a temple; God has said he will dwell in thick darkness ('arafel); and 6 more.

Only in The change of qibla: The direction of prayer (qibla) is changed toward the Sacred Mosque; fools ask why; Believers made a middle community (umma wasat), witnesses over mankind, with the messenger a witness over them; God sees the prophet turning his face toward heaven and grants him a qibla he is pleased with; To each a direction he faces: so race toward good deeds; Abraham and Ishmael pray that a messenger be raised from among their offspring; The People of the Book recognize the truth as they recognize their own sons; Leader prays 'remember me, my God, for good' for his deeds; Who bears witness to God's oneness [divergence between the texts].

passages.text: כִּֽי יֵצֵ֨א עַמְּךָ֤ לַמִּלְחָמָה֙ עַל א֣וֹיְבָ֔יו בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּשְׁלָחֵ֑ם וְהִתְפַּֽלְל֣וּ אֵלֶ֗יךָ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הָעִ֤יר הַזֹּאת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּחַ֣רְתָּ בָּ֔הּ וְהַבַּ֖יִת אֲשֶׁר בָּנִ֥יתִי לִשְׁמֶֽךָ

וְשָׁ֣בוּ אֵלֶ֗יךָ בְּכָל לִבָּם֙ וּבְכָל נַפְשָׁ֔ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ שִׁבְיָ֖ם אֲשֶׁר שָׁב֣וּ אֹתָ֑ם וְהִֽתְפַּֽלְל֗וּ דֶּ֤רֶךְ אַרְצָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תָּה לַאֲבוֹתָ֔ם וְהָעִיר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּחַ֔רְתָּ וְלַבַּ֖יִת אֲשֶׁר בָּנִ֥יתִי לִשְׁמֶֽךָ

قَدْ نَرَىٰ تَقَلُّبَ وَجْهِكَ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَلَنُوَلِّيَنَّكَ قِبْلَةً تَرْضَىٰهَا فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ وَحَيْثُ مَا كُنتُمْ فَوَلُّوا۟ وُجُوهَكُمْ شَطْرَهُۥ وَإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ لَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ ٱلْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمْ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا يَعْمَلُونَ
وَمِنْ حَيْثُ خَرَجْتَ فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ وَإِنَّهُۥ لَلْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكَ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ

وَمِنْ حَيْثُ خَرَجْتَ فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ وَحَيْثُ مَا كُنتُمْ فَوَلُّوا۟ وُجُوهَكُمْ شَطْرَهُۥ لِئَلَّا يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَيْكُمْ حُجَّةٌ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ مِنْهُمْ فَلَا تَخْشَوْهُمْ وَٱخْشَوْنِى وَلِأُتِمَّ نِعْمَتِى عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ

וְ֠אַתָּה תִּשְׁמַ֨ע מִן הַשָּׁמַ֜יִם מְכ֤וֹן שִׁבְתֶּ֨ךָ֙ וְסָ֣לַחְתָּ֔ וְנָתַתָּ֤ה לָאִישׁ֙ כְּכָל דְּרָכָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר תֵּדַ֖ע אֶת לְבָב֑וֹ כִּ֤י אַתָּה֙ לְבַדְּךָ֣ יָדַ֔עְתָּ אֶת לְבַ֖ב בְּנֵ֥י הָאָדָֽם

وَٱتَّبَعُوا۟ مَا تَتْلُوا۟ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينُ عَلَىٰ مُلْكِ سُلَيْمَٰنَ وَمَا كَفَرَ سُلَيْمَٰنُ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ يُعَلِّمُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ ٱلسِّحْرَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَى ٱلْمَلَكَيْنِ بِبَابِلَ هَٰرُوتَ وَمَٰرُوتَ وَمَا يُعَلِّمَانِ مِنْ أَحَدٍ حَتَّىٰ يَقُولَآ إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ فِتْنَةٌ فَلَا تَكْفُرْ فَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مِنْهُمَا مَا يُفَرِّقُونَ بِهِۦ بَيْنَ ٱلْمَرْءِ وَزَوْجِهِۦ وَمَا هُم بِضَآرِّينَ بِهِۦ مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مَا يَضُرُّهُمْ وَلَا يَنفَعُهُمْ وَلَقَدْ عَلِمُوا۟ لَمَنِ ٱشْتَرَىٰهُ مَا لَهُۥ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَٰقٍ وَلَبِئْسَ مَا شَرَوْا۟ بِهِۦٓ أَنفُسَهُمْ لَوْ كَانُوا۟ يَعْلَمُونَ

Only in Rules of war: exemptions, peace terms, fruit trees: Whether and when to call the enemy to peace [contrast between the texts]; Whether the enemy's trees may be cut down in a siege [contrast between the texts]; Who is excused from going out to war [contrast between the texts]; Who is excused from going out to war [divergence between the texts]; Ruling on soldiers who fear battle [contrast between the texts]; Men leave the battle line to go home, and how that is judged [contrast between the texts]; Exemptions from war for a new house, unharvested vineyard, betrothed bride, or faintheartedness [divergence between the texts]; Messengers offer peace terms before battle [divergence between the texts]; Peace offered or accepted in war, and its terms [divergence between the texts]; Book-people who aided the enemy are brought down from their fortresses, terror cast in their hearts; some killed, some captured, their land inherited; Priest addresses the army before battle: do not fear, God fights for you; City accepting peace becomes forced labor; one resisting has its males killed; and 10 more.

Only in New moons, fighting and the pilgrimage rites: When you pour down from Arafat, remember God at the Sacred Monument (al-Mash'ar al-Haram); Take provision, but the best provision is God-consciousness (taqwa); Remember God on the counted days; no sin whether one hastens in two days or delays; Piety is not entering houses from their backs but from their doors; Fight in God's way those who fight you, but do not transgress; Prayer 'Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the next, and guard us from the fire'; Complete the pilgrimage (hajj) and visitation (umra) for God; Do not fight at the Sacred Mosque unless they fight you there; No sexual talk, wickedness or quarreling during the pilgrimage; Remember God as you remember your fathers, or more; The sacred month for the sacred month; violations are subject to retaliation; Do not shave heads until the sacrificial offering (hady) reaches its place; and 10 more.

matches.note: Opposite rulings on the same case. leads.title: Arrival at Sinai, covenant offer and theophany ↔ Covenant at the mountain and the Sabbath-breakers
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 2 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The people's answer to the covenant ('we hear ...') [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Israel's position at the mountain when the covenant is made [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0). Pair score 12.7.

Only in Arrival at Sinai, covenant offer and theophany: Israel arrives at Sinai in the third month after leaving Egypt; God carried Israel on eagles' wings; Moses speaks and God answers him with a voice (thunder); God comes to the prophet in a thick cloud so the people may hear; Priests are mentioned before the Aaronic priesthood is instituted; A ram's horn blast signals that the people may go up the mountain; Men must not approach a woman before a holy encounter; God descends or reveals himself on the third day; A boundary is set round the holy mountain; whoever touches it dies; A horn blast at which all tremble [divergence between the texts]; Israel stands beneath the mountain when the covenant is given [divergence between the texts]; Israel is to be a kingdom of priests and a holy nation; and 9 more.

Only in Covenant at the mountain and the Sabbath-breakers: The Sabbath is an everlasting sign of the covenant between God and Israel; The people of the Sabbath were cursed and (some) made apes and swine; God raises the mountain (al-Tur) over Israel while taking their covenant; Formula 'no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve'; Punishment of those who break the Sabbath [divergence between the texts].

matches.note: Exod 19:17 wa-yyityaṣṣĕbû bĕ-taḥtît hā-hār: the people take their stand at the foot (lit. 'underneath') of the mountain; Q 2:63 wa-idh akhadhnā mīthāqakum wa-rafaʿnā fawqakumu ṭ-ṭūra khudhū mā ātaynākum bi-quwwatin: God raises the mountain above them as he takes the covenant. Standing below becomes the mountain held over them, and the free assent of Exod 19:8 (kōl ʾăšer dibber YHWH naʿăśeh) gives way to a command under the raised mountain. cf. b. Shabbat 88a for the same reading of taḥtît (rabbinic, not biblical).

leads.title: The Ten Words and the people's fear ↔ Polemic with the People of the Book
leads.summary: 2 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life (weight 5.3); Prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft and false witness (weight 5.1). Pair score 10.4.

Only in The Ten Words and the people's fear: God identifies himself as the one who brought Israel out of Egypt, the house of slaves; The people 'see' the voices or thunder at the revelation; Do not take God's name in vain; The prophet approaches the thick darkness where God is; Sexual relations with a neighbor's wife are forbidden [divergence between the texts]; Prohibition of coveting the neighbor's wife and property [divergence between the texts]; Do not kill the soul God has made sacred except by right [divergence between the texts]; No other gods before YHWH [divergence between the texts]; The ground and the reward of the duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; The Sabbath is justified by God's resting on the seventh day of creation; The Sabbath was imposed only on those who differed about it [response between the texts]; The Ten Commandments (Decalogue) [divergence between the texts]; and 12 more.

Only in Polemic with the People of the Book: The love of the calf was made to sink (be drunk) into their hearts; If the next world is yours alone, wish for death: they never will; Enmity to Gabriel and Michael (Mikal) equated with enmity to God; Gabriel (Jibril) brings down the revelation upon the prophet's heart; Some wish to be granted a life of a thousand years; Israel made to drink the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; Worship of God alone joined to duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; Claim that the fire will touch them only for a few numbered days, rebutted; The idol is burned, ground to powder, scattered on water and the people made to drink it; Israel at the mountain says 'we hear and we disobey' (sami'na wa-'asayna); Woe to those who write the book with their own hands and say it is from God, for a small price; Hypocrites profess faith before believers and tell their own 'devils' in private they were only mocking; and 15 more.

leads.title: Covenant Code - homicide, injury and the goring ox ↔ Retaliation and bequests
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 1 deliberately changed, 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: A negligent owner may pay a ransom for his life (weight 6.3); Retaliation (talion) for killing or injury [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); Eye for an eye, tooth for a tooth (lex talionis) (weight 5.4). Pair score 17.7.

Only in Covenant Code - homicide, injury and the goring ox: An animal that kills a person is stoned and its flesh not eaten; Men fighting strike a pregnant woman and she miscarries; One who injures another pays for his lost time and his healing; Whoever strikes a man so that he dies shall be put to death; A master who beats his slave to death is punished, unless the slave survives a day or two; Laws of the goring ox and the warned owner; A slave whose eye or tooth the master destroys goes free; Striking or cursing father or mother is a capital crime; The owner of an uncovered pit pays for an animal that falls in; A deliberate murderer is taken even from God's altar; Whether one who takes refuge at the sanctuary is safe [contrast between the texts]; A place of refuge for one who kills unintentionally; and 7 more.

Only in Retaliation and bequests: Kin of the slain may pardon and accept compensation (diya) instead of retaliation, a lightening from God; 'In retaliation there is life for you'; Retaliation (qisas) for the slain: free for free, slave for slave, female for female; Bequest (wasiyya) to parents and kin prescribed for one who leaves wealth; altering it is a sin; Whether payment may substitute for a life [contrast between the texts].

leads.title: Covenant Code - sorceress, stranger, widow, loans, firstborn ↔ Usury
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: To whom and how widely the ban on interest applies [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Do not charge interest to the poor of my people (weight 5.8). Pair score 12.1.

Only in Covenant Code - sorceress, stranger, widow, loans, firstborn: Lying with an animal is a capital crime; Whoever sacrifices to other gods is devoted to destruction; Flesh torn by beasts in the field is not eaten but thrown to dogs; Do not revile God or curse a ruler of your people; Flesh of an animal torn by a beast of prey is not to be eaten [divergence between the texts]; God hears the cry of the oppressed widow and orphan and punishes measure for measure; Newborn animal stays seven days with its mother before it may be sacrificed; Do not charge interest to the poor of my people [response between the texts]; Do not oppress the stranger, for you were strangers in Egypt; You shall not let a sorceress live; Firstborn sons and animals belong to God; A cloak taken in pledge must be returned before sunset; and 1 more.

Only in Usury: God blots out usury and makes charity grow; A debtor in hardship is given respite until ease; remitting it as charity is better; Trade is like usury, they say; but God permitted trade and forbade usury (riba); Those who consume usury rise like one driven mad by Satan's touch; Those who do not give up usury are warned of war from God and his messenger; they keep their principal; Whether obligations differ toward insiders and outsiders [contrast between the texts]; Relief of debtors: release or respite [divergence between the texts]; He who increases wealth by interest and usury gathers it for one who is gracious to the poor; Lending at interest or increase to a poor brother is forbidden.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: A bribe blinds the clear-sighted and perverts the words of the righteous (weight 5.6). Pair score 5.6.

Only in Covenant Code - justice, enemy's animal, sabbatical year, festivals: Return your enemy's stray animal and help his overloaded donkey; Neither favor nor pervert justice for the poor in his lawsuit; Whoever commits a sin and casts it on an innocent bears slander and manifest sin; God does not forbid kindness and justice toward those who did not fight you over religion or expel you; Do not offer sacrificial blood with leavened bread; fat not left until morning; No one shall appear before God empty-handed; Do not oppress the stranger, for you were strangers in Egypt; The land lies fallow in the seventh year for the poor and wild animals; Do not invoke the names of other gods; Let not hatred of a people move you to injustice; be just; Prohibition of boiling a kid in its mother's milk; Do not spread false reports or follow the majority to do wrong in court; and 6 more.

Only in The fast of Ramadan: Fasting prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you; Eat and drink until the white thread is distinguished from the black thread at dawn; Those able only with hardship may ransom fast days by feeding a poor person (fidya); Spouses not approached while in retreat (i'tikaf) in the mosques; Marital relations permitted on fast nights; spouses are garments for one another; Ramadan, the month in which the Quran was sent down; The sick and the traveler may make up missed fast days later; The wicked takes a bribe from the bosom to pervert the ways of justice; Marital relations during a fast [contrast between the texts]; What the annual fast is tied to [divergence between the texts]; Length, hours and exemptions of a prescribed fast [divergence between the texts]; 'These are the bounds (hudud) of God; do not approach (or transgress) them'; and 1 more.

Only in The burning bush and the divine name: God names himself 'I will be what I will be' (ehyeh asher ehyeh); God has seen the affliction, heard the cry and comes down to deliver; God introduced to a foreign king as 'the God of the Hebrews'; God foretells that the king will not let the people go except under compulsion; Hero hides his face, afraid to look at God; The sign confirming the call is that the people will later worship on this mountain; God calls Moses from the fire, from a bush or a tree [divergence between the texts]; God declares his name as his everlasting memorial for all generations; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; Whose forefathers' God is proclaimed in the Moses story [divergence between the texts]; How God names himself to Moses from the fire [divergence between the texts]; Formulaic list of the Canaanite, Hittite, Amorite, Perizzite, Hivite and Jebusite; and 16 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: People make a molten calf while the leader is on the mountain [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); God's pardon after the golden calf [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 13.4.

Only in The golden calf: Aaron builds an altar before the calf and proclaims a feast to YHWH; Intercessor reminds God of his oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; The people eat, drink and rise up to revel before the idol; The prophet's delay on the mountain makes the people lose faith; Whether the calf is a god that leads the people [response between the texts]; The calf is hailed as the god who brought Israel out of Egypt [divergence between the texts]; Israel asks its leader to make them a god [divergence between the texts]; God asks Moses why he hastened ahead of his people to the appointment [divergence between the texts]; The prophet intercedes for the people, arguing from God's reputation; A man called al-Sāmirī leads Israel astray and makes the calf [divergence between the texts]; Aaron's standing before God [divergence between the texts]; Who makes the golden calf and from what [divergence between the texts]; and 7 more.

Only in Exodus, the calf and the wilderness: Israelites who demanded to see God are struck by a thunderbolt and then raised after their death; Who or what parts the sea [divergence between the texts]; Israel's belief or disbelief in Moses after the sea [divergence between the texts]; The cloud over Israel in the wilderness: guide or shade [divergence between the texts]; Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt; Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt [divergence between the texts]; The killing of Israelites after the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; Wind brings quail in vast quantity to feed the people [divergence between the texts]; Humans seeing God [contrast between the texts]; People propose appointing a leader to go back to Egypt; Israel told to enter the town's gate prostrating and say 'hitta' (remission); the wrongdoers change the word; Ruler orders the killing of male infants [divergence between the texts]; and 16 more.

matches.note: Exod 32:27 kōh ʾāmar YHWH ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl ... wĕ-hirgû ʾîš ʾet ʾāḥîw: the Levites alone kill about three thousand of their brothers and are ordained for it (32:29 milʾû yedkem ha-yyôm); Q 2:54 fa-tūbū ilā bāriʾikum fa-qtulū anfusakum ... fa-tāba ʿalaykum: the killing is commanded to the whole people as their repentance, and ends in God's forgiveness. leads.title: Tablets broken, calf destroyed, Levites slaughter, Moses' offer ↔ Polemic with the People of the Book
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Israel made to drink the golden calf [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The idol is burned, ground to powder, scattered on water and the people made to drink it (weight 6.7). Pair score 13.4.

Only in Tablets broken, calf destroyed, Levites slaughter, Moses' offer: Aaron excuses himself: the people pressed him and the calf came out of the fire; The people run wild and become a derision to their enemies; God strikes the people with plague for idolatry; The prophet asks to be blotted from God's book if the people are not forgiven; The noise of the idolatrous revelry is mistaken for the sound of battle; The tablets are written on both sides by God; The leader calls 'Who is for YHWH? To me!' and a group rallies; Aaron answers Moses' rebuke over the calf [divergence between the texts]; Calf burned, ground to dust, and the dust thrown into the stream [divergence between the texts]; The calf-maker is condemned to say all his life 'No touching!' (lā misās), an outcast [divergence between the texts]; God erases what he wills and confirms, and with him is the Mother of the Book (umm al-kitab); God sends an angel ahead of Israel who bears God's name; and 15 more.

Only in Polemic with the People of the Book: The love of the calf was made to sink (be drunk) into their hearts; If the next world is yours alone, wish for death: they never will; Enmity to Gabriel and Michael (Mikal) equated with enmity to God; Gabriel (Jibril) brings down the revelation upon the prophet's heart; Some wish to be granted a life of a thousand years; Worship of God alone joined to duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; Claim that the fire will touch them only for a few numbered days, rebutted; Israel at the mountain says 'we hear and we disobey' (sami'na wa-'asayna); Woe to those who write the book with their own hands and say it is from God, for a small price; Hypocrites profess faith before believers and tell their own 'devils' in private they were only mocking; Jesus son of Mary given clear signs and supported with the holy spirit (ruh al-qudus); Michael, 'one of the chief princes', the great prince who stands over Israel; and 15 more.

leads.title: Mourning, the tent outside the camp, and Moses sees God's back ↔ Exodus, the calf and the wilderness
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: No human can see God's face and live (weight 5.8). Pair score 5.8.

Only in Mourning, the tent outside the camp, and Moses sees God's back: God refuses to go among the people lest he consume them on the way; Joshua, the young attendant, never leaves the tent; God tells the prophet: I know you by name and you have found favor; The people strip off their ornaments in mourning or penitence; The people stand at their tent doors and bow as the prophet goes to meet God; A tent of meeting pitched outside the camp where all who seek God go; God's own Presence (face) will go with the people; God declares he will be gracious to whom he will be gracious; Moses asks to see God, his glory or God himself [divergence between the texts]; God called Moses and drew him near in confidential converse (najiyy); Moses travels with his young servant (fata); After the calf the people mourn or repent of what they did [divergence between the texts]; and 10 more.

Only in Exodus, the calf and the wilderness: Israelites who demanded to see God are struck by a thunderbolt and then raised after their death; Who or what parts the sea [divergence between the texts]; Israel's belief or disbelief in Moses after the sea [divergence between the texts]; The cloud over Israel in the wilderness: guide or shade [divergence between the texts]; Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt; Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt [divergence between the texts]; God's pardon after the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; People make a molten calf while the leader is on the mountain [divergence between the texts]; The killing of Israelites after the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; Wind brings quail in vast quantity to feed the people [divergence between the texts]; Humans seeing God [contrast between the texts]; People propose appointing a leader to go back to Egypt; and 17 more.

leads.title: New tablets, the attributes of mercy and the ritual decalogue ↔ New moons, fighting and the pilgrimage rites
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: How often and when pilgrimage is made [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Three annual pilgrimage festivals when every male appears before God (weight 5.3). Pair score 11.6.

Only in New tablets, the attributes of mercy and the ritual decalogue: God promises no one will covet the land while the men go up on pilgrimage; The Sabbath must be kept even in plowing and harvest time; Call to the People of the Book to a common word: worship none but God and take none as lords besides him; What the tablets given at Sinai contain [divergence between the texts]; Israel must tear down the standing stones of the Canaanite gods; A firstborn donkey is redeemed with a lamb or its neck is broken; God passes by and proclaims his name and attributes of mercy; A boundary is set round the holy mountain; whoever touches it dies; Whether one person (kin, descendants) bears another's sin [contrast between the texts]; Make no covenant with the inhabitants or their gods, who would be a snare; Do not offer sacrificial blood with leavened bread; fat not left until morning; No one shall appear before God empty-handed; and 20 more.

Only in New moons, fighting and the pilgrimage rites: When you pour down from Arafat, remember God at the Sacred Monument (al-Mash'ar al-Haram); Take provision, but the best provision is God-consciousness (taqwa); Remember God on the counted days; no sin whether one hastens in two days or delays; Piety is not entering houses from their backs but from their doors; Fight in God's way those who fight you, but do not transgress; Prayer 'Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the next, and guard us from the fire'; Complete the pilgrimage (hajj) and visitation (umra) for God; Do not fight at the Sacred Mosque unless they fight you there; No sexual talk, wickedness or quarreling during the pilgrimage; Remember God as you remember your fathers, or more; The sacred month for the sacred month; violations are subject to retaliation; Do not shave heads until the sacrificial offering (hady) reaches its place; and 9 more.

leads.title: Bezalel makes the ark, table, lampstand and incense altar ↔ Talut (Saul), the ark and Jalut (Goliath)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The ark of the covenant: a gold-plated acacia chest with rings and poles (weight 5.6). Pair score 5.6.

Only in Bezalel makes the ark, table, lampstand and incense altar: A cult object is hammered from a single piece of gold; Recipe of the holy anointing oil of myrrh, cinnamon, cane, cassia and olive oil; A golden cover (kapporet, mercy seat) on top of the ark; Execution of a divine command is narrated by repeating the command almost verbatim; A small gold-plated altar for burning incense before the veil; A golden seven-lamp lampstand with almond-blossom cups; A gold table with the bread of the presence always before God; Two golden cherubim face each other with wings spread over the ark.

Only in Talut (Saul), the ark and Jalut (Goliath): The ark (tabut) returns, carried by angels, containing tranquility (sakina) and relics left by the family of Moses and Aaron; David kills Jalut (Goliath) and is given kingship and wisdom; Were it not for God checking people by means of others, the earth would be corrupted; 'How many a small band has overcome a large one by God's leave'; God chose the king and increased him in knowledge and stature, though he lacked wealth; The people object that the chosen king has no wealth and they have more right to kingship; Before battle the army is tested at a river: whoever drinks is not with the leader, except a handful scooped by hand; The ark of the covenant: a gold-plated acacia chest with rings and poles [divergence between the texts]; What the ark contains [contrast between the texts]; David kills the Philistine giant [divergence between the texts]; A giant taunts Israel and is killed by a hero; A jar of manna preserved before the testimony for future generations; and 10 more.

leads.title: The cauldron saying, death of Pelatiah, God as little sanctuary, the new heart, the glory on the Mount of Olives ↔ The cow and the slain man
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Hearts of stone [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); God will remove the heart of stone and give a heart of flesh and a new spirit (weight 5.8). Pair score 12.1.

Only in The cauldron saying, death of Pelatiah, God as little sanctuary, the new heart, the glory on the Mount of Olives: A man dies suddenly while the prophet is still prophesying against him; Proverb 'the city is the cauldron and we are the meat', turned against its speakers; God himself becomes 'a little sanctuary' (miqdash me'at) for the exiles in the lands of dispersion; The spirit carries the prophet back to the exiles and the vision lifts from him; Prophet falls on his face crying 'Ah Lord, will you destroy the whole remnant of Israel?'; The divine glory leaves the temple in stages: from the cherub to the threshold, to the east gate, to the mountain east of the city; Formula 'and you/they shall know that I am YHWH' closing a judgment or salvation oracle; God will gather the dispersed from the peoples and give them back the land of Israel; Formula 'I will take you as my people and I will be your God'.

Only in The cow and the slain man: Moses commands a cow be slaughtered; the people repeatedly ask its age, color and nature before complying; Hearts harder than stones, yet some stones gush rivers, split for water or fall down in fear of God; A slain man is struck with part of the slaughtered cow and revived to reveal his killer; The sacrificial cow is bright yellow, pleasing to beholders; What contact with a corpse does [contrast between the texts]; Unyoked milk cows pull a new cart unguided, separated from their calves, as a divine test; Description of the cow required by God [divergence between the texts]; A heifer and a killing whose perpetrator is unknown [divergence between the texts]; Unblemished red cow never yoked is burned whole for purifying ash; Unsolved murder: elders of nearest city break the neck of an unworked heifer in an untilled wadi.

leads.title: Sour grapes - individual responsibility and repentance ↔ Closing confession and prayer
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: 'The soul that sins, it shall die': the son does not bear the father's iniquity nor the father the son's (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Sour grapes - individual responsibility and repentance: Exhortation: cast away your transgressions and make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit; why will you die?; Test case of three generations: righteous father, violent son, and a grandson who sees his father's sins and does not imitate them; Whether one person can carry another's sin [divergence between the texts]; No one may excuse himself on judgment day because his ancestors associated partners; If the wicked turns from his sins, none of his transgressions will be remembered; if the righteous turns away, his righteousness is forgotten; Catalogue of the righteous man: no eating on the mountains, no idols, no adultery, no menstrual intercourse, no oppression, returns pledges, feeds the hungry, clothes the naked, no interest; Proverb 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes and the children's teeth are set on edge', abolished by God; Whether repentance has a time limit [divergence between the texts]; People complain 'the way of the Lord is not fair'; God answers that it is their ways that are unfair; God does not desire the death of the wicked but that he turn from his way and live; A cloak taken in pledge must be returned before sunset; Whoever does good does it for his own soul; whoever does evil, it is against it; and 4 more.

Only in Closing confession and prayer: Prayer not to be laid with a burden (isr) like that laid on those before us; Prayer to be cleansed of hidden and unwitting faults (shegi'ot, nistarot); Believers make no distinction between any of the prophets (Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Tribes, Moses, Jesus); 'We are the clay and you are our potter; we are all the work of your hand'; Believers' confession 'we hear and we obey' (sami'na wa-ata'na); God tests the hearts and the kidneys (inner self); God burdens no soul beyond its capacity; God alone knows the hearts of all humans.

leads.title: Israel's history of rebellion from Egypt; the second exodus into the wilderness of the peoples ↔ Covenant at the mountain and the Sabbath-breakers
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The Sabbath is an everlasting sign of the covenant between God and Israel (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Israel's history of rebellion from Egypt; the second exodus into the wilderness of the peoples: The people's wish 'We will be like the nations, serving wood and stone' will never come to pass; Wordplay etiology: 'What is the high place (bamah) to which you go (ha-ba'im)?' and its name is Bamah to this day; God refrains from destroying the people 'for the sake of my name', lest it be profaned in the sight of the nations; God swears he will not be inquired of by the elders who come to consult him; God swears 'with a mighty hand, outstretched arm and poured-out wrath I will be king over you'; Israel already worshipped the idols of Egypt in Egypt and would not cast them away; God makes the people pass under the shepherd's rod and brings them into the bond (masoret) of the covenant, purging out rebels; On God's holy mountain, the height of Israel, all Israel will serve him and he will accept their offerings as a pleasing odor; God will bring the exiles into 'the wilderness of the peoples' and judge them face to face as he judged the fathers in Egypt's wilderness; God gave the rebellious generation 'statutes that were not good and ordinances by which they could not live', defiling them through offering their firstborn; The person who does God's statutes shall live by them; Elders of the people come and sit before the prophet in his house to inquire; and 8 more.

Only in Covenant at the mountain and the Sabbath-breakers: The people's answer to the covenant ('we hear ...') [divergence between the texts]; The people of the Sabbath were cursed and (some) made apes and swine; Israel's position at the mountain when the covenant is made [divergence between the texts]; God raises the mountain (al-Tur) over Israel while taking their covenant; Formula 'no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve'; Punishment of those who break the Sabbath [divergence between the texts].

leads.title: For my holy name - clean water, new heart, my spirit within; the land like Eden ↔ The cow and the slain man
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Only in For my holy name - clean water, new heart, my spirit within; the land like Eden: Onlookers say 'This desolate land has become like the garden of Eden'; The exiles profane God's holy name among the nations, who say 'These are YHWH's people, yet they had to leave his land'; Israel's conduct defiled the land 'like the uncleanness of a menstruous woman'; God will multiply the people like flocks of men, like the holy flocks of Jerusalem at her appointed feasts; God declares 'Not for your sake do I act, O house of Israel, but for my holy name which you profaned'; God will sprinkle clean water upon them and purify them from all their uncleanness and idols; God will put his own spirit within them and cause them to walk in his statutes; The people's hearts are called hard (Arabic q-s-w, Hebrew q-sh-h), or God makes them so [divergence between the texts]; The land is impure with the impurity (niddah) of its peoples, filled from end to end; Survivors in exile will remember God, loathe themselves for their abominations and know he did not speak in vain; God is to be sanctified in the midst of Israel; his holy name not profaned; God will gather the dispersed from the peoples and give them back the land of Israel; and 1 more.

leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Deity creates by spoken command (Let there be...) (weight 5.8); God creates by saying to a thing 'Be' and it is (kun fa-yakun) (weight 5.3). Pair score 11.1.

Only in Creation in six days and the seventh-day rest: Deity gives names to the elements it creates (day, night, heaven, earth, seas); Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it; The earth itself is commanded to bring forth plants or animals; Light exists before the sun and moon are made; Humans and animals originally given only plants as food; Creation proceeds by dividing (light/darkness, waters above/below); Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it [divergence between the texts]; A divine wind or spirit hovers or moves over the primeval waters; God made every living thing from water [divergence between the texts]; God speaks to heavenly beings about making man [divergence between the texts]; The heavens and earth were a closed-up mass (ratq) that God split apart (fatq) [divergence between the texts]; The form God gave humans at creation [divergence between the texts]; and 26 more.

Only in Ra'ina, abrogation, rival claims and the face of God: Jews say the Christians stand on nothing, Christians say the same of the Jews; Claim that none enters paradise unless Jew or Christian, rebutted by surrender of the face to God; Believers told not to say 'ra'ina' (a word twisted by opponents) but 'unzurna'; God abrogates or causes to be forgotten a verse and brings a better or similar one (naskh); God swears by himself: to me every knee shall bow and every tongue swear; Whether God has or begets a son [contrast between the texts]; Whether God should speak to the people directly [contrast between the texts]; From sunrise to sunset God's name is great among the nations and in every place incense and a pure offering are brought to his name; East and west belong to God; wherever you turn, there is the face of God; 'He spoke and it came to be; he commanded and it stood firm'; The called one asks for a sign that it is God who speaks [divergence between the texts]; The called one asks for a sign that it is God who speaks; and 1 more.

leads.title: The covenant between the pieces ↔ Abraham and the four birds
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 2 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Abraham takes and cuts animals at God's command [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Covenant ritual: animals cut in halves and a divine presence passes between them (weight 6.3); The called one asks for a sign that it is God who speaks [divergence between the texts] (weight 5.8). Pair score 18.7.

Only in The covenant between the pieces: Birds of prey descend on the sacrifice and the hero drives them away; Childless patriarch's household servant is to be his heir; A great dark dread falls on the visionary at sunset; A people's guilt must reach its full measure before judgment; A smoking oven and flaming torch represent God's presence; Abraham looks at the stars, and why [divergence between the texts]; Promised land stretches from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates; God takes the patriarch outside and tells him to count the stars; God takes the patriarch outside and tells him to count the stars [divergence between the texts]; Descendants foretold to be enslaved in a foreign land 400 years and leave with great wealth; Patriarch believes God and it is counted to him as righteousness; God casts a deep sleep (tardemah) on a man; and 4 more.

Only in Abraham and the four birds: Abraham, asking to see how God revives the dead, takes four birds, places parts on each hill, calls them and they come flying; The called one asks for a sign that it is God who speaks.

matches.note: Gen 15:9-11, 17 qĕḥâ lî ʿeglâ mĕšulleševet ... wĕ-tōr wĕ-gôzāl ... wa-yĕbattēr ʾōtām ... wĕ-ʾet ha-ṣṣippōr lōʾ bātār ... wa-yyēred hā-ʿayiṭ ʿal ha-ppĕgārîm: heifer, goat, ram and two birds, the animals halved but the birds not; birds of prey come down and Abraham drives them off; a smoking oven passes between the pieces; Q 2:260 fa-khudh arbaʿatan mina ṭ-ṭayri fa-ṣurhunna ilayka thumma jʿal ʿalā kulli jabalin minhunna juzʾan thumma dʿuhunna yaʾtīnaka saʿyan: 'take four birds' (the command form qaḥ / khudh), cut them up, put a part on each hill, call them and they come running. leads.title: El Shaddai, new names and the covenant of circumcision ↔ Abraham, Ishmael and the House
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 1 deliberately changed, 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: A nation descended from Ishmael [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Whether and how God's covenant with Abraham passes to his offspring [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 13.4.

Only in El Shaddai, new names and the covenant of circumcision: Ishmael circumcised at thirteen, Abraham at ninety-nine; Uncircumcised male is cut off from his people; Circumcision commanded as the sign of the covenant; Circumcision on the eighth day after birth; Ishmael promised to father twelve princes and a great nation; Kings promised to come from the patriarch or matriarch; God changes a person's name to mark a new destiny; God promises to make the patriarch a great nation; God reveals himself by the name El Shaddai; Patriarch or matriarch laughs at the promise of a child in old age; God promises the land to the patriarch's descendants; A divine messenger announces a son's birth and gives his name.

Only in Abraham, Ishmael and the House: Abraham and Ishmael raise the foundations of the House while praying; Abraham told 'Submit' answers 'I submit to the Lord of the worlds' (aslamtu); God tests Abraham with words, he fulfills them and is made an imam for mankind; the covenant excludes the wrongdoers among his seed; The 'dye' or baptism (sibgha) of God: who has a better dye than God?; That was a community that has passed; it has what it earned and you what you earned; Dying Jacob asks his sons 'What will you worship after me?' and they confess the God of their fathers; Abraham and Ishmael pray that a messenger be raised from among their offspring; The chain of patriarchs to whom revelation or covenant passed [divergence between the texts]; The list of fathers in 'God of your fathers' [divergence between the texts]; Whether Ishmael is with Abraham or sent away [contrast between the texts]; Dying Jacob addresses his sons [divergence between the texts]; On that day no soul will avail another, no intercession or ransom accepted, no help given; and 16 more.

matches.note: Gen 17:20 û-lĕ-yišmāʿēʾl šĕmaʿtîkā ... ûnĕtattîw lĕ-gôy gādôl: Ishmael's line will be a great nation, outside the covenant (17:21); Q 2:128 wa-min dhurriyyatinā ummatan muslimatan laka: Abraham and Ishmael ask for a submitting community (umma) from their offspring. passages.text: וּֽלְיִשְׁמָעֵ֘אל שְׁמַעְתִּיךָ֒ הִנֵּ֣ה בֵּרַ֣כְתִּי אֹת֗וֹ וְהִפְרֵיתִ֥י אֹת֛וֹ וְהִרְבֵּיתִ֥י אֹת֖וֹ בִּמְאֹ֣ד מְאֹ֑ד שְׁנֵים עָשָׂ֤ר נְשִׂיאִם֙ יוֹלִ֔יד וּנְתַתִּ֖יו לְג֥וֹי גָּדֽוֹל
رَبَّنَا وَٱجْعَلْنَا مُسْلِمَيْنِ لَكَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِنَآ أُمَّةً مُّسْلِمَةً لَّكَ وَأَرِنَا مَنَاسِكَنَا وَتُبْ عَلَيْنَآ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ

matches.label: Whether and how God's covenant with Abraham passes to his offspring
matches.note: Gen 17:7 wa-hăqimōtî ʾet bĕrîtî bênî û-bênekā û-bên zarʿăkā ʾaḥărêkā ... li-bĕrît ʿôlām, and 17:19, 21 wĕ-ʾet bĕrîtî ʾāqîm ʾet yiṣḥāq: an everlasting covenant with Abraham's seed through Isaac; Q 2:124 qāla wa-min dhurriyyatī qāla lā yanālu ʿahdī ẓ-ẓālimīn: Abraham asks for his offspring and is told the covenant does not pass to the wrongdoers among them. Inherited covenant vs covenant by conduct.

passages.text: וַהֲקִמֹתִ֨י אֶת בְּרִיתִ֜י בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵינֶ֗ךָ וּבֵ֨ין זַרְעֲךָ֧ אַחֲרֶ֛יךָ לְדֹרֹתָ֖ם לִבְרִ֣ית עוֹלָ֑ם לִהְי֤וֹת לְךָ֙ לֵֽאלֹהִ֔ים וּֽלְזַרְעֲךָ֖ אַחֲרֶֽיךָ
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים אֲבָל֙ שָׂרָ֣ה אִשְׁתְּךָ֗ יֹלֶ֤דֶת לְךָ֙ בֵּ֔ן וְקָרָ֥אתָ אֶת שְׁמ֖וֹ יִצְחָ֑ק וַהֲקִמֹתִ֨י אֶת בְּרִיתִ֥י אִתּ֛וֹ לִבְרִ֥ית עוֹלָ֖ם לְזַרְע֥וֹ אַחֲרָֽיו
וְאֶת בְּרִיתִ֖י אָקִ֣ים אֶת יִצְחָ֑ק אֲשֶׁר֩ תֵּלֵ֨ד לְךָ֤ שָׂרָה֙ לַמּוֹעֵ֣ד הַזֶּ֔ה בַּשָּׁנָ֖ה הָאַחֶֽרֶת
وَإِذِ ٱبْتَلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِۦمَ رَبُّهُۥ بِكَلِمَٰتٍ فَأَتَمَّهُنَّ قَالَ إِنِّى جَاعِلُكَ لِلنَّاسِ إِمَامًا قَالَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِى قَالَ لَا يَنَالُ عَهْدِى ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

leads.title: Second creation account, Eden, and the making of woman ↔ Adam, the angels and Iblis
leads.summary: 3 correspondences read side by side: 3 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The garden given to the first humans to live and eat in [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The first man names the animals (weight 6.7); The first man and the names of the creatures [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The tree forbidden to the first humans [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); A tree of knowledge whose fruit is forbidden (weight 5.8); God plants a garden (Eden) in the east and places the first human there (weight 5.6). Pair score 38.1.

Only in Second creation account, Eden, and the making of woman: Eating the forbidden fruit is threatened with death; The first human is put in the garden to work and guard it; Man leaves father and mother and cleaves to his wife; they become one flesh; A mist or spring rises from the earth to water the ground; First couple naked and not ashamed; God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve [divergence between the texts]; Whether the first couple were naked or clothed before the fall [contrast between the texts]; How the first human's mate is made from the first human [divergence between the texts]; Whether any fruit in the Garden is forbidden [contrast between the texts]; Forming a creature from earth and breathing life into it [divergence between the texts]; Four rivers in the Garden [divergence between the texts]; In the garden Adam will not hunger, be naked, thirst or suffer the sun's heat [divergence between the texts]; and 16 more.

Only in Adam, the angels and Iblis: God teaches Adam all the names and he recites them to the angels, who cannot; The expelled are told 'Go down, enemies to one another' with a dwelling and provision on earth for a time; God announces to the angels he will place a vicegerent (khalifa) on earth; Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; Enmity decreed at the expulsion from the garden [divergence between the texts]; The first man's response after the transgression in the garden (blame or repentance) [divergence between the texts]; God speaks to heavenly beings about making man [divergence between the texts]; The human condition on earth after the expulsion [divergence between the texts]; The office given to humans on earth at creation [divergence between the texts]; The tempter in the garden [divergence between the texts]; Whoever sheds human blood, by man shall his blood be shed, because humans bear God's image; and 7 more.

matches.label: The first man and the names of the creatures
matches.note: Who knows the names is reversed. Gen 2:19 wa-yyābēʾ ʾel hā-ʾādām lirʾôt mah yyiqrāʾ lô ... wa-yyiqrāʾ hā-ʾādām šēmôt: God brings the animals 'to see what he would call them' and the man invents the names; Q 2:31 wa-ʿallama ādama l-asmāʾa kullahā thumma ʿaraḍahum ʿalā l-malāʾikati: God teaches Adam all the names and displays the creatures to the angels as a test, ending innī aʿlamu ghayba s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍ (2:33). Human initiative before an observing God becomes knowledge given by an all-knowing God, and the scene becomes a contest with the angels.

passages.text: וַיִּצֶר֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֜ים מִן הָֽאֲדָמָ֗ה כָּל חַיַּ֤ת הַשָּׂדֶה֙ וְאֵת֙ כָּל ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיָּבֵא֙ אֶל הָ֣אָדָ֔ם לִרְא֖וֹת מַה יִּקְרָא ל֑וֹ וְכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִקְרָא ל֧וֹ הָֽאָדָ֛ם נֶ֥פֶשׁ חַיָּ֖ה ה֥וּא שְׁמֽוֹ
וַיִּקְרָ֨א הָֽאָדָ֜ם שֵׁמ֗וֹת לְכָל הַבְּהֵמָה֙ וּלְע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וּלְכֹ֖ל חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה וּלְאָדָ֕ם לֹֽא מָצָ֥א עֵ֖זֶר כְּנֶגְדּֽוֹ

leads.title: Second creation account, Eden, and the making of woman ↔ Call to worship the Creator; the challenge; paradise and the gnat
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Paradise as gardens (of ʿAdn) beneath which rivers flow, where the righteous abide forever (weight 4.4). Pair score 4.4.

Only in Second creation account, Eden, and the making of woman: Eating the forbidden fruit is threatened with death; The first human is put in the garden to work and guard it; Man leaves father and mother and cleaves to his wife; they become one flesh; A mist or spring rises from the earth to water the ground; First couple naked and not ashamed; God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve [divergence between the texts]; The first man names the animals; Whether the first couple were naked or clothed before the fall [contrast between the texts]; The first man and the names of the creatures [divergence between the texts]; How the first human's mate is made from the first human [divergence between the texts]; Whether any fruit in the Garden is forbidden [contrast between the texts]; The tree forbidden to the first humans [divergence between the texts]; and 21 more.

Only in Call to worship the Creator; the challenge; paradise and the gnat: God is not ashamed to strike a parable of a gnat or something smaller; Fruits in paradise resemble those of earth: 'this is what we were given before'; A challenge to rivals to prove a divine claim [divergence between the texts]; God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; The people break the covenant God made with them; Humans were dead, given life, will die and be given life again (two deaths, two lives); God stretches out the heavens like a tent curtain; Hell's fire has men and stones as its fuel; The blessed have purified spouses (azwaj mutahhara) in paradise; God summons the coastlands and nations (and their gods) to a court trial to argue their case; God fashions seven heavens; Inimitability challenge: produce a surah like it, calling on your own witnesses (tahaddi); and 2 more.

Only in Birth of Isaac and expulsion of Hagar and Ishmael: Mother lays her dying child under a bush and sits a bowshot away weeping; Slave-wife and her son expelled at the wife's demand; The outcast son grows up in the wilderness as an archer; A great feast on the day the child is weaned; God opens a woman's eyes to see a well in the desert that saves her child; Promised son born to aged parents at the appointed time; In labor the mother wishes she had died before this and been utterly forgotten; Abraham settles some of his offspring in a barren valley by God's sacred House [divergence between the texts]; When and why Sarah laughs, and how it is answered; Mistreated slave-woman flees or is sent into the wilderness; Abraham thanks God for giving him Ishmael and Isaac in old age [divergence between the texts]; Circumcision on the eighth day after birth; and 4 more.

matches.note: Gen 22:1 wĕ-hā-ʾĕlōhîm nissâ ʾet ʾabrāhām, ending 22:18 wĕ-hitbārăkû bĕ-zarʿăkā kōl gôyê hā-ʾāreṣ ʿēqeb ʾăšer šāmaʿtā bĕ-qōlî; Q 2:124 wa-idhi btalā ibrāhīma rabbuhu bi-kalimātin fa-atammahunna qāla innī jāʿiluka li-n-nāsi imāman. God tests Abraham (nissâ / ibtalā) and the reward reaches all peoples (kōl gôyê hā-ʾāreṣ / li-n-nās). But the test is unnamed 'words', not the binding of a son; the reward is to be an imam for mankind; and the blessing on the seed is limited: lā yanālu ʿahdī ẓ-ẓālimīn 'my covenant does not reach the wrongdoers' among his offspring.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Patriarch reaps a hundredfold in one year (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Isaac in Gerar, the wife-sister episode, wells and treaty: God forbids the patriarch to go down to Egypt in a famine; King looking through a window sees the couple embracing and learns they are married; Successive wells named for strife (Esek, Sitnah) and finally room (Rehoboth); Enemies stop up the patriarch's wells with earth out of envy; Abraham's relation to the law given later at Sinai [response between the texts]; Whether Abraham had a written revelation, or kept God's laws unwritten [divergence between the texts]; Abraham kept God's charge, commandments, statutes and laws (torot) before Sinai; Seven ewe lambs given as witness to a well-ownership oath (Beersheba); Dispute over a well resolved by an oath-treaty with a local king; The foreign king rebukes the patriarch for the deception; Patriarch passes off his beautiful wife as his sister in a foreign court; Patriarch builds an altar where God appeared to him; and 6 more.

Only in Parables of charity: Charity voided by reminders of generosity and injury, like dust on a rock washed bare by rain; Spending for God's pleasure is like a garden on a height that yields double with heavy rain or even with dew; Spending in God's way is like a grain sprouting seven ears with a hundred grains each; Deserving poor, restrained in God's way, thought rich by the ignorant for their restraint, known by their mark; Satan threatens you with poverty and commands indecency; Advice to break off sins by righteousness/almsgiving (tsidqah) and iniquities by mercy to the poor; He who gives to the poor will not lack, but he who hides his eyes will get many curses; An old man with weak children loses his garden of palms and vines to a fiery whirlwind; Giving charity openly is good, but giving it secretly to the poor is better and expiates sins; God gives wisdom to whom he wills; whoever is given wisdom is given much good; One scatters and yet increases; the generous soul is made fat and who waters will be watered.

leads.title: The serpent, the eating, the curses and the expulsion ↔ Adam, the angels and Iblis
leads.summary: 6 correspondences read side by side: 5 deliberately changed, 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The tempter in the garden [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Enmity decreed at the expulsion from the garden [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The first man's response after the transgression in the garden (blame or repentance) [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The human condition on earth after the expulsion [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); First humans expelled from the garden [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); First humans expelled from the garden (weight 6.0); A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit (weight 6.0); God speaks in the plural (us, our) as if to a divine council (weight 6.0); A tree of knowledge whose fruit is forbidden (weight 5.8). Pair score 56.8.

Only in The serpent, the eating, the curses and the expulsion: Each accused shifts blame to another (man to woman, woman to serpent); First woman named as mother of all living; God heard walking in the garden in the breeze of the day; Humans gain divine knowledge and God fears they will also gain immortality; Woman punished with pain in childbirth and subordination to husband; The woman eats first and gives the fruit to her husband; Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness [divergence between the texts]; Cherubim and a flaming turning sword guard the way to the tree of life; Eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked [divergence between the texts]; How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts]; God makes garments of skin for the first couple; God makes garments of skin for the first couple [divergence between the texts]; and 18 more.

Only in Adam, the angels and Iblis: God teaches Adam all the names and he recites them to the angels, who cannot; The expelled are told 'Go down, enemies to one another' with a dwelling and provision on earth for a time; God announces to the angels he will place a vicegerent (khalifa) on earth; The first man names the animals; Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; The first man and the names of the creatures [divergence between the texts]; The tree forbidden to the first humans [divergence between the texts]; The garden given to the first humans to live and eat in [divergence between the texts]; God speaks to heavenly beings about making man [divergence between the texts]; The office given to humans on earth at creation [divergence between the texts]; Whoever sheds human blood, by man shall his blood be shed, because humans bear God's image; and 4 more.

passages.text: וְהַנָּחָשׁ֙ הָיָ֣ה עָר֔וּם מִכֹּל֙ חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל הָ֣אִשָּׁ֔ה אַ֚ף כִּֽי אָמַ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֔ים לֹ֣א תֹֽאכְל֔וּ מִכֹּ֖ל עֵ֥ץ הַגָּֽן
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים לָאִשָּׁ֖ה מַה זֹּ֣את עָשִׂ֑ית וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה הַנָּחָ֥שׁ הִשִּׁיאַ֖נִי וָאֹכֵֽל
فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ وَقُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ

matches.label: First humans expelled from the garden
matches.note: Gen 3:23-24 wa-yšallĕḥēhû YHWH ʾĕlōhîm ... wa-ygāreš ʾet hā-ʾādām, with cherubim and a flaming sword guarding the tree of life: God drives the man out; Q 2:36 fa-akhrajahumā mimmā kānā fīhi: Satan is the subject who 'brought them out', then God's ihbiṭū 'go down' (2:36, 2:38), addressed to a plural. No cherubim, no tree of life.

passages.text: וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵ֛הוּ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים מִגַּן עֵ֑דֶן לַֽעֲבֹד֙ אֶת הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֻקַּ֖ח מִשָּֽׁם
וַיְגָ֖רֶשׁ אֶת הָֽאָדָ֑ם וַיַּשְׁכֵּן֩ מִקֶּ֨דֶם לְגַן עֵ֜דֶן אֶת הַכְּרֻבִ֗ים וְאֵ֨ת לַ֤הַט הַחֶ֨רֶב֙ הַמִּתְהַפֶּ֔כֶת לִשְׁמֹ֕ר אֶת דֶּ֖רֶךְ עֵ֥ץ הַֽחַיִּֽים
فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ وَقُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ
قُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ مِنْهَا جَمِيعًا فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ

matches.label: Enmity decreed at the expulsion from the garden
matches.note: Gen 3:15 wĕ-ʾêbâ ʾāšît bênkā û-bên hā-ʾiššâ û-bên zarʿăkā û-bên zarʿāh: enmity between serpent and woman and their offspring; Q 2:36 ihbiṭū baʿḍukum li-baʿḍin ʿaduwwun: 'some of you enemies to others' among those sent down. The same decree of enmity (ʾêbâ / ʿaduww) at the expulsion, with the serpent gone.

passages.text: וְאֵיבָ֣ה אָשִׁ֗ית בֵּֽינְךָ֙ וּבֵ֣ין הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וּבֵ֥ין זַרְעֲךָ֖ וּבֵ֣ין זַרְעָ֑הּ ה֚וּא יְשׁוּפְךָ֣ רֹ֔אשׁ וְאַתָּ֖ה תְּשׁוּפֶ֥נּוּ עָקֵֽב
فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ وَقُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ

matches.label: The human condition on earth after the expulsion
matches.note: Gen 3:17-19 ʾărûrâ hā-ʾădāmâ baʿăbûrekā bĕ-ʿiṣṣābôn tōʾkălennâ ... ʿad šûbĕkā ʾel hā-ʾădāmâ: cursed ground, toil and death; Q 2:36 wa-lakum fī l-arḍi mustaqarrun wa-matāʿun ilā ḥīn: on earth an abode and provision for a time. The curses on ground, woman and serpent are left out; the earth is a lodging and a time limit, not a curse.

passages.text: וּלְאָדָ֣ם אָמַ֗ר כִּֽי שָׁמַעְתָּ֮ לְק֣וֹל אִשְׁתֶּךָ֒ וַתֹּ֨אכַל֙ מִן הָעֵ֔ץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר צִוִּיתִ֨יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֥א תֹאכַ֖ל מִמֶּ֑נּוּ אֲרוּרָ֤ה הָֽאֲדָמָה֙ בַּֽעֲבוּרֶ֔ךָ בְּעִצָּבוֹן֙ תֹּֽאכֲלֶ֔נָּה כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיֶּֽיךָ
בְּזֵעַ֤ת אַפֶּ֨יךָ֙ תֹּ֣אכַל לֶ֔חֶם עַ֤ד שֽׁוּבְךָ֙ אֶל הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה כִּ֥י מִמֶּ֖נָּה לֻקָּ֑חְתָּ כִּֽי עָפָ֣ר אַ֔תָּה וְאֶל עָפָ֖ר תָּשֽׁוּב
فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ وَقُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ

matches.label: The first man's response after the transgression in the garden (blame or repentance)
matches.note: The ending changes. Gen 3:12 hā-ʾiššâ ʾăšer nātattâ ʿimmādî hîʾ nātĕnâ-llî min hā-ʿēṣ wā-ʾōkēl: the man blames the woman (and God who gave her), with no repentance or pardon; Q 2:37 fa-talaqqā ādamu min rabbihi kalimātin fa-tāba ʿalayhi innahu huwa t-tawwābu r-raḥīm: Adam receives words and God turns to him in forgiveness before the descent. The Quran adds a reconciliation Genesis does not have.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הָֽאָדָ֑ם הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תָּה עִמָּדִ֔י הִ֛וא נָֽתְנָה לִּ֥י מִן הָעֵ֖ץ וָאֹכֵֽל
فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَٰتٍ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ

matches.label: A tree of knowledge whose fruit is forbidden
matches.note: Q 2:35 wa-lā taqrabā hādhihi sh-shajarata 'do not come near this tree' is God's own wording; in Genesis the extension is the woman's addition: Gen 3:3 lōʾ tōʾkĕlû mimmennû wĕ-lōʾ tiggĕʿû bô 'nor touch it', which God had not said (2:17).

passages.text: וּמִפְּרִ֣י הָעֵץ֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּתוֹךְ הַגָּן֒ אָמַ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֗ים לֹ֤א תֹֽאכְלוּ֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְלֹ֥א תִגְּע֖וּ בּ֑וֹ פֶּן תְּמֻתֽוּן
وَقُلْنَا يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسْكُنْ أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ وَكُلَا مِنْهَا رَغَدًا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

matches.label: A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit

passages.text: וְהַנָּחָשׁ֙ הָיָ֣ה עָר֔וּם מִכֹּל֙ חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל הָ֣אִשָּׁ֔ה אַ֚ף כִּֽי אָמַ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֔ים לֹ֣א תֹֽאכְל֔וּ מִכֹּ֖ל עֵ֥ץ הַגָּֽן
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַנָּחָ֖שׁ אֶל הָֽאִשָּׁ֑ה לֹֽא מ֖וֹת תְּמֻתֽוּן

leads.title: Restoration of Jacob and the taunt over the king of Babylon (Helel son of Dawn) ↔ Abraham disputes with the king
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Abraham disputes with a king, who claims 'I give life and death' (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Restoration of Jacob and the taunt over the king of Babylon (Helel son of Dawn): The proud one plans to ascend to heaven, raise his throne above the stars of El and make himself like Elyon; Reversal: Israel will take captive those who captured them and rule over their oppressors; The would-be god is brought down instead to Sheol, to the recesses of the pit (yarkete bor); Strangers (gerim) will join themselves to Israel and cleave to the house of Jacob; 'How you have fallen from heaven, Helel son of Shahar (Shining One, son of Dawn)!' - a star-figure cast down to earth; In the underworld maggots are spread beneath the dead king and worms are his covering; The mount of assembly (har mo'ed) in the recesses of the north (yarkete tsafon), seat of the gods; God cuts off from the enemy 'name and remnant, offspring and posterity'; Sheol below is stirred to meet the arriving tyrant; the shades and dead kings rise from their thrones to greet him: 'you too have become weak like us'; God sweeps the city with the broom of destruction, leaving it to hedgehogs and marshes; Mocking dirge (mashal) over a fallen tyrant: 'How the oppressor has ceased!'; The cypresses and cedars of Lebanon rejoice that no woodcutter comes up since the tyrant fell; and 8 more.

leads.title: Woe to Ariel; enemies like a dream; the sealed book; lip service; the potter and the clay ↔ Believers, unbelievers and hypocrites
leads.summary: 4 correspondences read side by side: 1 opposite ruling, 2 same element, 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Revelation as a sealed or an open book [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.7); The hypocrites try to deceive God, but it is he who deceives them (weight 6.3); This people honors God with lips while its heart is far; its fear of him is a commandment of men learned by rote (weight 6.0); God sets a seal on the unbelievers' hearts and hearing and a covering over their eyes (weight 5.3). Pair score 24.3.

Only in Woe to Ariel; enemies like a dream; the sealed book; lip service; the potter and the clay: Jerusalem called 'Ariel' (altar-hearth / lion of God), the city where David camped, to be besieged and become 'like an ariel'; The multitude of nations fighting Zion will be like a dream of the night: like a hungry man who dreams he eats and wakes empty; YHWH 'who redeemed Abraham' (a deliverance of Abraham alluded to); Vision is like a sealed book: the literate cannot read it because it is sealed, the illiterate because he cannot read; God pours out a spirit of deep sleep (tardemah) and shuts the eyes of prophets and seers; The humbled city's voice will come from the ground like a ghost's (ov) and chirp from the dust; God will do wonders so that the wisdom of the wise perishes and the understanding of the prudent is hidden; They hide from people but not from God, who is with them when they plot by night; In a little while Lebanon will become a fruitful field (Carmel) and the field be counted a forest; Shall the clay say to the potter 'he did not make me' or 'he has no understanding'?; The people's reckoning draws near while they turn away in heedlessness; God seals the sleepers' ears (puts them to sleep) in the cave for many years; and 8 more.

Israel sees much but does not observe; Hypocrites profess faith before believers and tell their own 'devils' in private they were only mocking; Who is called blind and deaf toward God's word [divergence between the texts]; God in heaven laughs at and mocks those who plot against him or the righteous; and 2 more.

leads.title: Trial of the nations; the one from the east; Israel my servant, fear not; gods challenged to foretell ↔ Call to worship the Creator; the challenge; paradise and the gnat
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: A nation's sorcerers, enchanters, star-gazers and monthly prognosticators are challenged and cannot save it (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Taunt over the virgin daughter Babylon: Virgin daughter Babylon is made to come down from her throne and sit in the dust; A proud city says in her heart 'I am, and there is none besides me' and is brought low; The wrongdoer says 'No one sees me', trusting in secrecy; The proud city personified as a lady is made a slave-girl who grinds meal, removes her veil, bares her legs and wades rivers; The wicked or their helpers become like stubble burned up by fire; The city that said 'I shall not sit as a widow nor know bereavement' suffers both in one day; A personified city or nation punished by having her nakedness and skirts uncovered.

Only in Solomon, the devils and Harut and Marut: Devils (shayatin) taught sorcery in Solomon's reign; Solomon himself did not disbelieve; Two angels in Babylon, Harut and Marut, teach magic while warning 'we are only a trial'; Magic is learned that separates a man from his wife, harming only by God's leave; Whether Solomon turned from God [response between the texts]; Divination, soothsaying, mediums (ov) and wizards (yidde'oni) are forbidden; The king's experts cannot interpret the dream.

leads.title: Song of the vineyard; six woes; the nation from afar ↔ Believers, unbelievers and hypocrites
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, darkness light and bitter sweet (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Song of the vineyard; six woes; the nation from afar: Woe to those who rise early for strong drink and feast with lyre and harp but ignore God's work; God raises a banner and whistles for a nation from the ends of the earth to come as his instrument; Woe to those who join house to house and field to field until there is no room left; Parable-song of the beloved's vineyard that yielded wild grapes despite all care and is abandoned to briars; The invading army never tires, sleeps or loosens belt or sandal; its horses' hooves like flint, its roar like a lion; Prophetic paronomasia: hoped for mishpat (justice) but got mishpah (bloodshed), for tsedaqah but got tse'aqah (outcry); God speaks to the snow 'Fall on the earth' and commands the downpour; Hypocrite men and women enjoin wrong and forbid right and close their hands; Refrain: 'For all this his anger is not turned back and his hand is stretched out still'; Sheol enlarges its appetite and opens its mouth without limit to swallow the people; God sends the flood of al-'Arim (the dam) and turns the two gardens into bitter fruit, tamarisk and a few lote-trees; Scoffers ask 'Lord, hasten to us our share (qittana) before the Day of Reckoning'; and 8 more.

Only in Believers, unbelievers and hypocrites: The faithful defined as those who believe in the unseen (al-ghayb); The scripture announces itself as 'the Book' in which there is no doubt, guidance for the God-fearing; Unbelievers called 'deaf, dumb, blind' (summun bukmun umyun); Parable: one kindles a fire, and when it lights his surroundings God takes away the light, leaving him in darkness; Parable: travelers in a rainstorm of darkness, thunder and lightning put fingers in their ears for fear of death; God scorns the scorners but gives grace to the humble; Hardening of the heart, ears and eyes of the hearers [divergence between the texts]; Revelation as a sealed or an open book [contrast between the texts]; Who is blind but my servant, deaf like my messenger? Israel sees much but does not observe; The hypocrites try to deceive God, but it is he who deceives them; Hypocrites profess faith before believers and tell their own 'devils' in private they were only mocking; Who is called blind and deaf toward God's word [divergence between the texts]; and 5 more.

leads.title: The fast that God chooses; the Sabbath a delight ↔ Lawful food and true piety
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Piety (birr) is not turning faces east or west but faith, giving wealth to kin, orphans, poor, travelers, beggars and captives (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in The fast that God chooses; the Sabbath a delight: When the righteous call, God answers 'Here I am' (hinneni); The prophet is told to cry aloud and lift his voice like a ram's horn; The restorer is called 'repairer of the breach, restorer of paths to dwell in'; Call the Sabbath a delight (oneg), refraining from one's own business and idle talk on it; The righteous become like a watered garden and a spring whose waters never fail; The people complain 'Why have we fasted and you do not see?' and are rebuked; The fast God chooses is to loose bonds of injustice, free the oppressed, share bread with the hungry and clothe the naked; Mourner puts on sackcloth and ashes and cries aloud in public.

Only in Lawful food and true piety: Those who conceal scripture for gain eat only fire into their bellies; Refusal of revelation in favor of what was found with the fathers is rebuked; Wealth given for (freeing) necks, i.e. ransoming slaves and captives; Unbelievers are like beasts shouted at by a herdsman, hearing only a call and a cry; Appeal to the religion of the fathers [contrast between the texts]; The pig is unclean and forbidden [divergence between the texts]; Rule on eating an animal that died of itself [contrast between the texts]; Eating an animal that died or was torn requires washing and makes unclean until evening; Forbidden: what has been consecrated (invoked over) to other than God; Eating blood is forbidden [divergence between the texts]; Forbidden food is permitted to one compelled by necessity, without desire or transgression; Eating blood is forbidden; and 1 more.

passages.text: הֲל֣וֹא זֶה֮ צ֣וֹם אֶבְחָרֵהוּ֒ פַּתֵּ֨חַ֙ חַרְצֻבּ֣וֹת רֶ֔שַׁע הַתֵּ֖ר אֲגֻדּ֣וֹת מוֹטָ֑ה וְשַׁלַּ֤ח רְצוּצִים֙ חָפְשִׁ֔ים וְכָל מוֹטָ֖ה תְּנַתֵּֽקוּ

leads.title: The throne vision and the call of Isaiah ↔ Believers, unbelievers and hypocrites
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 1 deliberately changed, 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Hardening of the heart, ears and eyes of the hearers [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Prophet commissioned to make the people's heart fat, ears heavy and eyes shut lest they understand and be healed (weight 5.0). Pair score 11.7.

Only in The throne vision and the call of Isaiah: A seraph touches the prophet's lips with a burning coal from the altar, removing his guilt; Six-winged seraphim stand above God: two wings cover the face, two the feet, two for flying; Even the tenth that remains will be burned, like a felled terebinth or oak whose stump is the holy seed; At the heavenly voice the doorposts shake and the house fills with smoke; Prophet sees the Lord seated on a high and lifted-up throne, his train filling the temple; Heavenly beings call 'Holy, holy, holy is YHWH of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory'; God asks 'Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?' and the prophet volunteers 'Here am I, send me'; Prophet cries 'Woe is me, I am undone, a man of unclean lips' for having seen the King; The angels say: each of us has a known station; we are ranged in ranks; we glorify; God has not given the people a heart to know, eyes to see, ears to hear until today [divergence between the texts]; God is 'Lord of the mighty Throne' (rabb al-'arsh al-'azim); The prophet's word and a people deaf and blind to it [divergence between the texts]; and 10 more.

Only in Believers, unbelievers and hypocrites: The faithful defined as those who believe in the unseen (al-ghayb); The scripture announces itself as 'the Book' in which there is no doubt, guidance for the God-fearing; Unbelievers called 'deaf, dumb, blind' (summun bukmun umyun); Parable: one kindles a fire, and when it lights his surroundings God takes away the light, leaving him in darkness; Parable: travelers in a rainstorm of darkness, thunder and lightning put fingers in their ears for fear of death; Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, darkness light and bitter sweet; God scorns the scorners but gives grace to the humble; Revelation as a sealed or an open book [contrast between the texts]; Who is blind but my servant, deaf like my messenger? Israel sees much but does not observe; The hypocrites try to deceive God, but it is he who deceives them; Hypocrites profess faith before believers and tell their own 'devils' in private they were only mocking; Who is called blind and deaf toward God's word [divergence between the texts]; and 4 more.

leads.finding: Hardening of the heart, ears and eyes of the hearers

units.title: The throne vision and the call of Isaiah
Believers, unbelievers and hypocrites

matches.label: Hardening of the heart, ears and eyes of the hearers
matches.note: Same triad in the same order: Isa 6:10 hašmēn lēb hā-ʿām ... wĕ-ʾoznāyw hakbēd wĕ-ʿênāyw hāšaʿ (heart, ears, eyes); Q 2:7 khatama llāhu ʿalā qulūbihim wa-ʿalā samʿihim wa-ʿalā abṣārihim ghishāwatun (hearts, hearing, eyes). Who acts changes: in Isaiah the prophet is ordered to do the hardening (imperatives to Isaiah); in the Quran God himself seals, and the prophet's role is only that his warning makes no difference (sawāʾun ʿalayhim a-andhartahum am lam tundhirhum, 2:6).

passages.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֵ֥ךְ וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ לָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמ֨וֹעַ֙ וְאַל תָּבִ֔ינוּ וּרְא֥וּ רָא֖וֹ וְאַל תֵּדָֽעוּ
הַשְׁמֵן֙ לֵב הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה וְאָזְנָ֥יו הַכְבֵּ֖ד וְעֵינָ֣יו הָשַׁ֑ע פֶּן יִרְאֶ֨ה בְעֵינָ֜יו וּבְאָזְנָ֣יו יִשְׁמָ֗ע וּלְבָב֥וֹ יָבִ֛ין וָשָׁ֖ב וְרָ֥פָא לֽוֹ
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَأَنذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنذِرْهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ
خَتَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ وَعَلَىٰ سَمْعِهِمْ وَعَلَىٰٓ أَبْصَٰرِهِمْ غِشَٰوَةٌ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ

matches.label: Prophet commissioned to make the people's heart fat, ears heavy and eyes shut lest they understand and be healed
matches.note: Isa 6:10 pen ... ûlĕbābô yābîn wā-šāb wĕ-rāpāʾ lô 'lest it understand, turn and be healed'; Q 2:18 fa-hum lā yarjiʿūn 'so they do not turn back' and 2:10 fī qulūbihim maraḍun fa-zādahumu llāhu maraḍan 'disease in their hearts, and God increased it': the turning (šûb / rajaʿa) and the healing (rāpāʾ) of Isaiah reappear as no return and a disease God increases.

passages.text: הַשְׁמֵן֙ לֵב הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה וְאָזְנָ֥יו הַכְבֵּ֖ד וְעֵינָ֣יו הָשַׁ֑ע פֶּן יִרְאֶ֨ה בְעֵינָ֜יו וּבְאָזְנָ֣יו יִשְׁמָ֗ע וּלְבָב֥וֹ יָבִ֛ין וָשָׁ֖ב וְרָ֥פָא לֽוֹ
فِى قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ فَزَادَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مَرَضًا وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌۢ بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَكْذِبُونَ
صُمٌّۢ بُكْمٌ عُمْىٌ فَهُمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ

leads.title: Remembering the days of Moses - O that you would rend the heavens ↔ Closing confession and prayer
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
