leads.title: Cursed who trusts in man, blessed who trusts in YHWH; the deceitful heart ↔ Closing confession and prayer
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God tests the hearts and the kidneys (inner self) (weight 5.6). Pair score 5.6.

Only in Cursed who trusts in man, blessed who trusts in YHWH; the deceitful heart: Cursed is the man who trusts in man and makes flesh his arm; he is like a juniper in the desert, in a salt land; 'A glorious throne, exalted from the beginning, is the place of our sanctuary'; The heart is deceitful ('aqov) above all things and desperately sick; who can know it?; Those who turn away from God will be written in the earth (or dust), for they forsook the fountain of living water; Like a partridge that hatches eggs it did not lay is one who gets riches unjustly; he will leave them in the middle of his days; Leader contrasts the enemy's 'arm of flesh' with God who fights for us; Parable: a bad word is like a bad tree uprooted from the earth, with no stability; The people forsook God, the fountain of living waters, and dug broken cisterns that hold no water; The rich man thinks his garden will never perish and the Hour will never come; The righteous man is like a tree planted by streams of water, bearing fruit in season, leaf never withering.

Only in Closing confession and prayer: Prayer not to be laid with a burden (isr) like that laid on those before us; Prayer to be cleansed of hidden and unwitting faults (shegi'ot, nistarot); Believers make no distinction between any of the prophets (Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Tribes, Moses, Jesus); 'The soul that sins, it shall die': the son does not bear the father's iniquity nor the father the son's; 'We are the clay and you are our potter; we are all the work of your hand'; Believers' confession 'we hear and we obey' (sami'na wa-ata'na); God burdens no soul beyond its capacity; God alone knows the hearts of all humans.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Only in What is the burden of YHWH?: When asked 'What is the burden (massa) of YHWH?' the prophet answers 'You are the burden, and I will cast you off'; the phrase is banned; YHWH is the true God, the living God and everlasting King at whose wrath the earth quakes; God did not send the prophets who promise peace; they prophesy a lying vision, divination and the deceit of their heart; God made the people a horror, a desolation and a hissing.

leads.title: Can a divorced wife return? Faithless Israel, treacherous Judah ↔ Oaths, divorce, nursing and widowhood
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Divorced wife who remarried may not return to her first husband (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Can a divorced wife return? Faithless Israel, treacherous Judah: In the future the ark of the covenant will no longer be spoken of, remembered, missed or made again; The apostate people sat waiting for lovers by the roads like an Arab in the wilderness; Jerusalem will be called the throne of YHWH and all nations will gather to it; God will take the returnees 'one from a city and two from a family' and bring them to Zion; The houses of Judah and Israel will walk together and come from the land of the north; Two sister nations (Israel and Judah) are both unfaithful wives; the second fails to learn from the first's divorce; God is the father who acquired, made and established his people; God will give shepherds after his own heart who feed the people with knowledge; A name containing Baal replaced by boshet ('shame'); God calls 'Return, faithless children (shuvu banim shovavim), I will heal your faithlessness'; Husband writes a bill of divorcement for 'some indecency' and sends her away; Exiles confess their own iniquity and that of their fathers; and 3 more.

Only in Oaths, divorce, nursing and widowhood: Divorce is twice; then retain honorably or release with kindness; Divorced women wait three menstrual periods (quru') and may not conceal what is in their wombs; Do not prevent divorced women from remarrying their husbands when agreed; Do not retain divorced wives to harm them; Husband may not take back what he gave the wife except in fear of transgressing God's bounds; If divorced before consummation with dower fixed, half the dower is due; No blame if the wife ransoms herself (khul') when they fear not keeping God's bounds; Proposal may be hinted during the waiting period but no secret promise or contract until it ends; Oath of abstention from wives (ila'): a four-month waiting period; In fear, pray on foot or riding; Divorced women are due a provision (mut'a) according to the husband's means; After a third divorce she may not return to the first husband until she marries another; and 12 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Only in Ambush and capture of Ai; altar and Torah inscribed on Mount Ebal: Leader holds out his javelin and does not lower his hand until victory is complete; A captured enemy king is killed and hanged on a tree until sunset, then buried under stones; Large stones plastered with lime and inscribed with the whole Torah after crossing; The whole law is read aloud before the assembly, including women, children and foreigners; Column of smoke from the city is the prearranged signal of the ambush; Blessing pronounced on Mount Gerizim and curse on Mount Ebal; A great heap of stones is raised over an executed man, 'to this day'; Altar of whole stones on which no iron tool is lifted; Feigned retreat draws defenders out while an ambush takes the city; Ban (herem): total destruction of a conquered population.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Only in Angel calls Gideon at the winepress; fire from the rock; YHWH-shalom: The angel of YHWH sits under a sacred tree before calling the hero; The one called asks where God's wonders are if God is with us; The angel touches the offering with his staff and fire from the rock consumes it; The hero is called while secretly at work (threshing wheat in a winepress); A man prepares a meal for a divine visitor; The angel greets the hero: YHWH is with you, mighty man of valor; An altar is given a name containing the divine name; Witness fears he will die because he has seen God or an angel; The called prophet raises objections (who am I, they won't believe, I can't speak, send someone else); Litany of divine names: King, Holy, Peace, Faithful, Guardian, Mighty, Compeller, Proud, Creator, Maker, Fashioner; to him belong the most beautiful names.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Length, hours and exemptions of a prescribed fast [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in The appointed times - sabbath and annual festivals: A holy day is kept from evening to evening; First sheaf (omer) of the harvest waved by the priest on the morrow after the sabbath; Two leavened loaves of new grain offered as first fruits; New bread, parched grain or fresh ears may not be eaten until the first sheaf is offered; Annual Day of Atonement on the tenth of the seventh month, with self-affliction and total rest; First day of the seventh month as a 'day of blasting' (yom teru'ah); An eighth day of solemn assembly ('atseret) closes the seven-day festival; Seven full weeks (fifty days) counted from the sheaf offering to the new grain offering; Fruit of a goodly tree, palm fronds, leafy boughs and brook willows taken for the festival; Calendar of festivals with prescribed offerings (Passover, Weeks, Trumpets, Atonement, Booths); Corners of the field, gleanings and fallen grapes left for the poor and the stranger; Passover on the fourteenth of the first month at twilight; and 3 more.

Only in The fast of Ramadan: Fasting prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you; Eat and drink until the white thread is distinguished from the black thread at dawn; Those able only with hardship may ransom fast days by feeding a poor person (fidya); Spouses not approached while in retreat (i'tikaf) in the mosques; Marital relations permitted on fast nights; spouses are garments for one another; Ramadan, the month in which the Quran was sent down; The sick and the traveler may make up missed fast days later; The wicked takes a bribe from the bosom to pervert the ways of justice; Marital relations during a fast [contrast between the texts]; What the annual fast is tied to [divergence between the texts]; 'These are the bounds (hudud) of God; do not approach (or transgress) them'; YHWH is near to all who call on him in truth; and 1 more.

leads.title: Redemption of land, interest-free loans, and Israelite bondmen ↔ Usury
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: To whom and how widely the ban on interest applies [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Lending at interest or increase to a poor brother is forbidden (weight 5.6). Pair score 11.9.

Only in Redemption of land, interest-free loans, and Israelite bondmen: An impoverished Israelite sold to a brother serves as a hired worker, not a slave, until the jubilee; Houses in Levite cities can always be redeemed and their fields never sold; Do not rule over a fellow Israelite with harshness (perekh); Permanent slaves may be bought from surrounding nations and resident aliens and bequeathed; A house in a walled city can be redeemed only within a year and does not return at the jubilee; Freeing or buying back the enslaved [divergence between the texts]; Sold land returns to its ancestral owner in the jubilee; Israelite sold to a resident alien may be redeemed by kin or himself, priced by years to jubilee; Whose slaves or servants the Israelites are [contrast between the texts]; Israelites cannot be sold as slaves because they are God's servants whom he brought out of Egypt; Nearest kinsman (go'el) has the right and duty to redeem land and family.

Only in Usury: God blots out usury and makes charity grow; A debtor in hardship is given respite until ease; remitting it as charity is better; Trade is like usury, they say; but God permitted trade and forbade usury (riba); Those who consume usury rise like one driven mad by Satan's touch; Those who do not give up usury are warned of war from God and his messenger; they keep their principal; Whether obligations differ toward insiders and outsiders [contrast between the texts]; Relief of debtors: release or respite [divergence between the texts]; He who increases wealth by interest and usury gathers it for one who is gracious to the poor; Do not charge interest to the poor of my people.

leads.title: Covenant curses, exile, and remembered covenant ↔ Polemic with the People of the Book
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The 'uncircumcised' or covered heart [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); The people's 'uncircumcised heart' must be humbled (weight 5.6). Pair score 11.9.

Only in Covenant curses, exile, and remembered covenant: Curse: your corpses will be heaped on the corpses of your idols; Punishments escalate sevenfold each time the people do not listen; Curse of consumption and fever that waste the eyes and the soul; Curse: you will flee though no one pursues, chased by the sound of a driven leaf; Curse: God will not smell the pleasing odor of their offerings; God answers the people's 'walking contrary' (qeri) by walking contrary to them; Curse: the sky like iron and the earth like bronze; Curse: ten women bake bread in one oven and it is doled out by weight; Humiliation is stamped on them wherever found except under a rope from God and a rope from men; While the people are in exile, the desolate land makes up its missed sabbath years; The people's 'uncircumcised heart' must be humbled [divergence between the texts]; Curse: you will eat the flesh of your sons and daughters; and 5 more.

Only in Polemic with the People of the Book: The love of the calf was made to sink (be drunk) into their hearts; If the next world is yours alone, wish for death: they never will; Enmity to Gabriel and Michael (Mikal) equated with enmity to God; Gabriel (Jibril) brings down the revelation upon the prophet's heart; Some wish to be granted a life of a thousand years; Israel made to drink the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; Worship of God alone joined to duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; Claim that the fire will touch them only for a few numbered days, rebutted; The idol is burned, ground to powder, scattered on water and the people made to drink it; Israel at the mountain says 'we hear and we disobey' (sami'na wa-'asayna); Woe to those who write the book with their own hands and say it is from God, for a small price; Hypocrites profess faith before believers and tell their own 'devils' in private they were only mocking; and 15 more.

leads.title: The well-being (shelamim) offering and the ban on fat and blood ↔ Lawful food and true piety
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Eating blood is forbidden [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Eating blood is forbidden (weight 5.6). Pair score 11.9.

Only in The well-being (shelamim) offering and the ban on fat and blood: All the fat belongs to YHWH; The sacrifice is called God's food (lehem); Priests dash the blood against all sides of the altar; The fat tail of the sheep is offered [divergence between the texts]; The well-being offering (shelamim), shared between altar, priest and offerer; Eating the fat (helev) of sacrificial animals is forbidden; The fat, the two kidneys and the lobe of the liver are burned on the altar; The fat tail of the sheep is offered; The offerer lays his hand on the head of the animal.

Only in Lawful food and true piety: Those who conceal scripture for gain eat only fire into their bellies; Refusal of revelation in favor of what was found with the fathers is rebuked; Wealth given for (freeing) necks, i.e. ransoming slaves and captives; Unbelievers are like beasts shouted at by a herdsman, hearing only a call and a cry; Appeal to the religion of the fathers [contrast between the texts]; The pig is unclean and forbidden [divergence between the texts]; Piety (birr) is not turning faces east or west but faith, giving wealth to kin, orphans, poor, travelers, beggars and captives; Rule on eating an animal that died of itself [contrast between the texts]; Eating an animal that died or was torn requires washing and makes unclean until evening; Forbidden: what has been consecrated (invoked over) to other than God; Forbidden food is permitted to one compelled by necessity, without desire or transgression; The pig is unclean and forbidden.

leads.title: Graduated purification offering and the guilt (asham) offering ↔ The debt verse
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: A witness who hears a public adjuration and withholds testimony bears guilt (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Graduated purification offering and the guilt (asham) offering: The poorest bring a flour sin offering without oil or frankincense; One is guilty even for a sin committed without knowing; Restitution to the wronged person precedes the atonement offering; Sacrilege (me'ilah) against the holy things of YHWH; Touching an unclean carcass or human impurity makes one guilty; Defrauding a neighbor with a false oath is a trespass against God; The priest pinches off the bird's head with his fingernail (melikah); Expiation in steps according to what one can afford [divergence between the texts]; The guilt offering is a ram assessed in silver shekels; The priest burns a handful as the token or 'memorial' portion (azkarah); Liability for oaths spoken thoughtlessly [contrast between the texts]; The priest makes atonement and the sinner is forgiven; and 8 more.

Only in The debt verse: A debt for a fixed term must be written by a just scribe, dictated by the debtor or his guardian; Two male witnesses, or one man and two women so that if one errs the other reminds her; On a journey without a scribe a pledge in hand (rihan maqbuda) is taken; A land deed made in a sealed copy and an open copy, witnessed and the silver weighed; How many witnesses are required [divergence between the texts]; No one put to death on the testimony of a single witness.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: From sunrise to sunset God's name is great among the nations and in every place incense and a pure offering are brought to his name (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Priests who despise God's name with blemished offerings: The altar is called 'the table of YHWH' and the offering 'bread' (lehem); God wishes someone would shut the temple doors rather than kindle the altar in vain; A son honors his father and a servant his master: 'If I am a father, where is my honor?'; God calls himself 'a great king' (melekh gadol) whose name is feared among the nations; 'Offer that to your governor; would he accept you?': sarcastic comparison of God and a human ruler; Disputation form: God states a claim, the people object 'How have you...?', and God answers; Blemished animal (lame, blind) may not be sacrificed.

Only in Ra'ina, abrogation, rival claims and the face of God: Jews say the Christians stand on nothing, Christians say the same of the Jews; Claim that none enters paradise unless Jew or Christian, rebutted by surrender of the face to God; Believers told not to say 'ra'ina' (a word twisted by opponents) but 'unzurna'; God abrogates or causes to be forgotten a verse and brings a better or similar one (naskh); God swears by himself: to me every knee shall bow and every tongue swear; Whether God has or begets a son [contrast between the texts]; Whether God should speak to the people directly [contrast between the texts]; East and west belong to God; wherever you turn, there is the face of God; 'He spoke and it came to be; he commanded and it stood firm'; Deity creates by spoken command (Let there be...); The called one asks for a sign that it is God who speaks [divergence between the texts]; The called one asks for a sign that it is God who speaks; and 2 more.

Only in The book of remembrance and the sun of righteousness: The day comes burning like an oven; the arrogant and evildoers become stubble, left neither root nor branch; Complaint: 'It is vain to serve God; what profit that we kept his charge? The arrogant are blessed and the wicked test God and escape'; God will spare the faithful as a man spares the son who serves him, on the day he makes his treasured possession; The righteous go out leaping like stall-fed calves and tread the wicked like ashes under their feet; For those who fear God the sun of righteousness will rise with healing in its wings (kenafeha); A book of remembrance is written before God for those who fear him and think on his name; There is no secret conversation of three but God is the fourth, nor of five but he is the sixth, wherever they are; God will not leave believers as they are until he separates the bad from the good; God's messengers (angels) write down what people plot and do; God records what people sent ahead and their traces (athar), and counts everything in a clear register (imam mubin); 'Why do the wicked live, grow old and mighty?': prosperity of the wicked with children, safe houses and fertile cattle; On judgment day people are either wretched (shaqi) or blessed (sa'id); and 2 more.

leads.title: Fast of the twenty-fourth and the Levites' historical confession ↔ Polemic with the People of the Book
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 2 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: People of the Book cast God's book behind their backs (weight 5.8); Israel killed the prophets who warned them (weight 5.1); People make a molten calf while the leader is on the mountain (weight 4.7). Pair score 15.6.

Only in Fast of the twenty-fourth and the Levites' historical confession: God found Abraham's heart faithful (ne'eman) before him; God chose Abram, brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans and renamed him Abraham; Call to bless God 'from everlasting to everlasting'; God's ordinances are those 'which a man shall do and live by them'; 'You give life to them all' - God sustains all creation; God gave his good spirit to instruct the people in the wilderness; Levites stand on a platform and cry out to God with a loud voice; A quarter of the day spent reading the Torah and a quarter confessing and bowing; God made known his holy Sabbath at Sinai; The seed of Israel separate themselves from all foreigners; Drowned enemies sink like a stone or like lead in mighty waters; Closing doxology: glory to your Lord, Lord of might, above what they describe; peace on the messengers; praise to God, Lord of the worlds; and 15 more.

Only in Polemic with the People of the Book: The love of the calf was made to sink (be drunk) into their hearts; If the next world is yours alone, wish for death: they never will; Enmity to Gabriel and Michael (Mikal) equated with enmity to God; Gabriel (Jibril) brings down the revelation upon the prophet's heart; Some wish to be granted a life of a thousand years; Israel made to drink the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; Worship of God alone joined to duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; Claim that the fire will touch them only for a few numbered days, rebutted; The idol is burned, ground to powder, scattered on water and the people made to drink it; Israel at the mountain says 'we hear and we disobey' (sami'na wa-'asayna); Woe to those who write the book with their own hands and say it is from God, for a small price; Hypocrites profess faith before believers and tell their own 'devils' in private they were only mocking; and 14 more.

passages.text: אַ֗ף כִּֽי עָשׂ֤וּ לָהֶם֙ עֵ֣גֶל מַסֵּכָ֔ה וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ זֶ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶעֶלְךָ֖ מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֔וּ נֶאָצ֖וֹת גְּדֹלֽוֹת

וַיְמָאֲנ֣וּ לִשְׁמֹ֗עַ וְלֹא זָכְר֤וּ נִפְלְאֹתֶ֨יךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֣יתָ עִמָּהֶ֔ם וַיַּקְשׁוּ֙ אֶת עָרְפָּ֔ם וַיִּתְּנוּ רֹ֛אשׁ לָשׁ֥וּב לְעַבְדֻתָ֖ם בְּמִרְיָ֑ם וְאַתָּה֩ אֱל֨וֹהַּ סְלִיח֜וֹת חַנּ֧וּן וְרַח֛וּם אֶֽרֶךְ אַפַּ֥יִם וְרַב וחסד חֶ֖סֶד וְלֹ֥א עֲזַבְתָּֽם

וְאַתָּה֙ בְּרַחֲמֶ֣יךָ הָֽרַבִּ֔ים לֹ֥א עֲזַבְתָּ֖ם בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר אֶת עַמּ֣וּד הֶ֠עָנָן לֹא סָ֨ר מֵעֲלֵיהֶ֤ם בְּיוֹמָם֙ לְהַנְחֹתָ֣ם בְּהַדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְאֶת עַמּ֨וּד הָאֵ֤שׁ בְּלַ֨יְלָה֙ לְהָאִ֣יר לָהֶ֔ם וְאֶת הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֵֽלְכוּ בָֽהּ
وَلَقَدْ جَآءَكُم مُّوسَىٰ بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ ثُمَّ ٱتَّخَذْتُمُ ٱلْعِجْلَ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ وَأَنتُمْ ظَٰلِمُونَ

وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَٰقَكُمْ وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَكُمُ ٱلطُّورَ خُذُوا۟ مَآ ءَاتَيْنَٰكُم بِقُوَّةٍ وَٱسْمَعُوا۟ قَالُوا۟ سَمِعْنَا وَعَصَيْنَا وَأُشْرِبُوا۟ فِى قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلْعِجْلَ بِكُفْرِهِمْ قُلْ بِئْسَمَا يَأْمُرُكُم بِهِۦٓ إِيمَٰنُكُمْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ

leads.title: Taberah, the craving, the seventy elders and the quail ↔ Exodus, the calf and the wilderness
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 2 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt (weight 6.7); Wind brings quail in vast quantity to feed the people [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Wind brings quail in vast quantity to feed the people (weight 5.8); The people grumble against their leaders about food or water (weight 5.1). Pair score 30.9.

Only in Taberah, the craving, the seventy elders and the quail: Fire from God burns part of the camp for complaint; Spirit rests on people and they prophesy (ecstatically); A 'rabble' or mixed crowd among the people instigates sin; Leader refuses to silence prophets outside the sanctioned place: 'would all were prophets'; Bird-meat as desired food: punished or granted [contrast between the texts]; Leader doubts God can supply; God replies 'Is my hand too short?' [divergence between the texts]; Craved food granted, then plague strikes while meat is still in their mouths; Leader protests he did not conceive or bear the people to carry them like a nurse; Exhausted leader asks God to kill him; Manna described: like coriander seed, look of bdellium, taste of oil cakes, falls with the dew; Seventy elders of Israel accompany or assist the prophet [divergence between the texts]; Some of the spirit on the leader is taken and placed on others; and 4 more.

Only in Exodus, the calf and the wilderness: Israelites who demanded to see God are struck by a thunderbolt and then raised after their death; Who or what parts the sea [divergence between the texts]; Israel's belief or disbelief in Moses after the sea [divergence between the texts]; The cloud over Israel in the wilderness: guide or shade [divergence between the texts]; God's pardon after the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; People make a molten calf while the leader is on the mountain [divergence between the texts]; The killing of Israelites after the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; Humans seeing God [contrast between the texts]; People propose appointing a leader to go back to Egypt; Israel told to enter the town's gate prostrating and say 'hitta' (remission); the wrongdoers change the word; Ruler orders the killing of male infants [divergence between the texts]; Moses strikes the rock for water [divergence between the texts]; and 13 more.

matches.note: Num 11:5 zākarnû ʾet ha-ddāgâ ... ʾēt ha-qqiššuʾîm wĕ-ʾēt hā-ʾăbaṭṭiḥîm wĕ-ʾet he-ḥāṣîr wĕ-ʾet ha-bbĕṣālîm wĕ-ʾet ha-ššûmîm; Q 2:61 baqlihā wa-qiththāʾihā wa-fūmihā wa-ʿadasihā wa-baṣalihā. Three cognates (qiššuʾîm / qiththāʾ, bĕṣālîm / baṣal, šûmîm / fūm). Changed: in Numbers the craving is for meat (mî yaʾăkilēnû bāśār, 11:4) and the food is remembered from Egypt; in the Quran the complaint is 'one food' (lan naṣbira ʿalā ṭaʿāmin wāḥidin), fish and meat are absent, lentils are added. The outcome changes too: plague in Num 11:33; in Q ihbiṭū miṣran fa-inna lakum mā saʾaltum, and humiliation.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God ranked some messengers above others; to some God spoke (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses: Hero called the humblest man on earth; Ordinary prophets receive revelation in visions and dreams; Afflicted person shut outside the camp seven days; Prophet's own siblings challenge his unique authority; Father spitting in a daughter's face brings seven days' shame; Believers must not put themselves before God and his messenger, nor raise their voices above the prophet's or shout to him; God speaks to one prophet 'mouth to mouth', not in dreams or riddles; Prophet criticized over his foreign (Cushite) wife; Moses asks his people: 'Why do you hurt me when you know I am God's messenger to you?'; when they swerved God made their hearts swerve; Those who hurt Moses: God cleared him of what they said [divergence between the texts]; How God speaks to prophets: face to face, in vision or dream, from behind a veil, or by a messenger [divergence between the texts]; Offender struck with skin disease 'white as snow'; and 2 more.

Only in Ranks of the messengers and the Throne Verse: God's footstool or seat (kursi) extends over the heavens and the earth; No compulsion in religion; Neither slumber nor sleep overtakes God; God's throne in relation to heaven and earth [divergence between the texts]; Whoever rejects false gods (taghut) and believes in God grasps the firmest handhold that never breaks; God does not slumber or sleep [divergence between the texts]; The guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps; A day comes with no trade, no friendship and no intercession; The temple as a house of rest for the ark and the footstool of God's feet; Jesus son of Mary given clear signs and supported with the holy spirit (ruh al-qudus); Israel's God is called 'the living God, enduring forever, whose kingdom shall never be destroyed'; God the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting (al-hayy al-qayyum); and 4 more.

leads.title: The red heifer and corpse impurity ↔ The cow and the slain man
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 1 deliberately changed, 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Unblemished red cow never yoked is burned whole for purifying ash (weight 6.7); Description of the cow required by God [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); What contact with a corpse does [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 20.1.

Only in The red heifer and corpse impurity: Ash mixed with running ('living') water sprinkled to cleanse; Those who prepare the purifying agent are themselves rendered impure; A corpse defiles everyone and every open vessel in the tent; Cedar wood, hyssop and scarlet thread used in a purification rite; Purification by sprinkling on the third and seventh days; Contact with a human corpse makes one ritually impure; Without water, purify with clean earth (tayammum), wiping face and hands; Blood or water sprinkled seven times; The offender 'shall be cut off from his people' (karet).

Only in The cow and the slain man: Moses commands a cow be slaughtered; the people repeatedly ask its age, color and nature before complying; Hearts harder than stones, yet some stones gush rivers, split for water or fall down in fear of God; A slain man is struck with part of the slaughtered cow and revived to reveal his killer; The sacrificial cow is bright yellow, pleasing to beholders; Unyoked milk cows pull a new cart unguided, separated from their calves, as a divine test; A heifer and a killing whose perpetrator is unknown [divergence between the texts]; Unsolved murder: elders of nearest city break the neck of an unworked heifer in an untilled wadi; Hearts of stone [divergence between the texts]; God will remove the heart of stone and give a heart of flesh and a new spirit.

matches.label: Description of the cow required by God
matches.note: Description point by point. Num 19:2 pārâ ʾădummâ tĕmîmâ ʾăšer ʾên bāh mûm ʾăšer lōʾ ʿālâ ʿālêhā ʿōl; Q 2:69, 2:71 baqaratun ṣafrāʾu fāqiʿun lawnuhā ... lā dhalūlun tuthīru l-arḍa wa-lā tasqī l-ḥartha musallamatun lā shiyata fīhā. Whole (tĕmîmâ / musallama), without blemish (ʾên bāh mûm / lā shiyata fīhā), never under the yoke (lōʾ ʿālâ ʿālêhā ʿōl / lā dhalūl): all match. The colour changes, red (ʾădummâ) to bright yellow (ṣafrāʾ fāqiʿ). The legal statute (ḥuqqat ha-ttôrâ) becomes a narrative in which the people haggle over the details (2:68-71).

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Moses strikes the rock for water [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); The people grumble against their leaders about food or water (weight 5.1). Pair score 11.4.

Only in Miriam's death; water from the rock at Meribah: Death and burial of the hero's sister; Leader strikes the rock (twice) instead of speaking to it; Water brought out of a rock by the leader's rod; Place called 'waters of strife' (Meribah); The great leader is denied entry into the promised land for a lapse.

Only in Exodus, the calf and the wilderness: Israelites who demanded to see God are struck by a thunderbolt and then raised after their death; Who or what parts the sea [divergence between the texts]; Israel's belief or disbelief in Moses after the sea [divergence between the texts]; The cloud over Israel in the wilderness: guide or shade [divergence between the texts]; Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt; Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt [divergence between the texts]; God's pardon after the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; People make a molten calf while the leader is on the mountain [divergence between the texts]; The killing of Israelites after the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; Wind brings quail in vast quantity to feed the people [divergence between the texts]; Humans seeing God [contrast between the texts]; People propose appointing a leader to go back to Egypt; and 16 more.

matches.label: Moses strikes the rock for water
matches.note: Num 20:8 wĕ-dibbartem ʾel ha-selaʿ: Moses is told to speak to the rock; he strikes it with his staff (20:11 wa-yyak ʾet ha-selaʿ bĕ-maṭṭēhû) and is barred from the land for it (20:12 yaʿan lōʾ heʾĕmantem bî). Q 2:60 fa-qulnā ḍrib bi-ʿaṣāka l-ḥajara: God himself orders the striking with the staff, so the act that is Moses' sin in Numbers is obedience in the Quran.

passages.text: קַ֣ח אֶת הַמַּטֶּ֗ה וְהַקְהֵ֤ל אֶת הָעֵדָה֙ אַתָּה֙ וְאַהֲרֹ֣ן אָחִ֔יךָ וְדִבַּרְתֶּ֧ם אֶל הַסֶּ֛לַע לְעֵינֵיהֶ֖ם וְנָתַ֣ן מֵימָ֑יו וְהוֹצֵאתָ֨ לָהֶ֥ם מַ֨יִם֙ מִן הַסֶּ֔לַע וְהִשְׁקִיתָ֥ אֶת הָעֵדָ֖ה וְאֶת בְּעִירָֽם
וַיָּ֨רֶם מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶת יָד֗וֹ וַיַּ֧ךְ אֶת הַסֶּ֛לַע בְּמַטֵּ֖הוּ פַּעֲמָ֑יִם וַיֵּצְאוּ֙ מַ֣יִם רַבִּ֔ים וַתֵּ֥שְׁתְּ הָעֵדָ֖ה וּבְעִירָֽם

וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָה֮ אֶל מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאֶֽל אַהֲרֹן֒ יַ֚עַן לֹא הֶאֱמַנְתֶּ֣ם בִּ֔י לְהַ֨קְדִּישֵׁ֔נִי לְעֵינֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לָכֵ֗ן לֹ֤א תָבִ֨יאוּ֙ אֶת הַקָּהָ֣ל הַזֶּ֔ה אֶל הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁר נָתַ֥תִּי לָהֶֽם

وَإِذِ ٱسْتَسْقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِۦ فَقُلْنَا ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلْحَجَرَ فَٱنفَجَرَتْ مِنْهُ ٱثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا قَدْ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ مَّشْرَبَهُمْ كُلُوا۟ وَٱشْرَبُوا۟ مِن رِّزْقِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ

leads.title: Vows of men and women ↔ Oaths, divorce, nursing and widowhood
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: How far a spoken oath or vow binds [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Vows of men and women: Silence on hearing counts as confirmation; Vows of a widow or divorced woman stand on their own; Father or husband may annul a woman's vow on the day he hears it; A man's vow or oath must be fulfilled as uttered; A man's vow or oath must be fulfilled as uttered [contrast between the texts].

Only in Oaths, divorce, nursing and widowhood: Divorce is twice; then retain honorably or release with kindness; Divorced women wait three menstrual periods (quru') and may not conceal what is in their wombs; Do not prevent divorced women from remarrying their husbands when agreed; Do not retain divorced wives to harm them; Husband may not take back what he gave the wife except in fear of transgressing God's bounds; If divorced before consummation with dower fixed, half the dower is due; No blame if the wife ransoms herself (khul') when they fear not keeping God's bounds; Proposal may be hinted during the waiting period but no secret promise or contract until it ends; Oath of abstention from wives (ila'): a four-month waiting period; In fear, pray on foot or riding; Divorced women are due a provision (mut'a) according to the husband's means; After a third divorce she may not return to the first husband until she marries another; and 12 more.

وَلَا تَجْعَلُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ عُرْضَةً لِّأَيْمَٰنِكُمْ أَن تَبَرُّوا۟ وَتَتَّقُوا۟ وَتُصْلِحُوا۟ بَيْنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ
لَّا يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِٱللَّغْوِ فِىٓ أَيْمَٰنِكُمْ وَلَٰكِن يُؤَاخِذُكُم بِمَا كَسَبَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ

leads.title: Levitical cities, cities of refuge and the law of homicide ↔ The debt verse
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: No one put to death on the testimony of a single witness (weight 5.4). Pair score 5.4.

Only in Levitical cities, cities of refuge and the law of homicide: Murder distinguished from manslaughter by weapon (iron, stone, wood), enmity and intent; Manslayer may leave refuge only at the death of the high priest; Shed blood pollutes the land and only the killer's blood atones for it; Forty-eight cities with pasture-lands of measured cubits assigned to the Levites; No ransom (kofer) may be taken for a murderer's life; How many witnesses a charge requires [divergence between the texts]; A place of refuge for one who kills unintentionally [divergence between the texts]; The 'redeemer of blood' (go'el ha-dam) kills the murderer; Same law for the resident alien and the native; Whether payment may substitute for a life [contrast between the texts]; Six cities of refuge for the unintentional killer, three on each side of the Jordan.

Only in The debt verse: A debt for a fixed term must be written by a just scribe, dictated by the debtor or his guardian; Two male witnesses, or one man and two women so that if one errs the other reminds her; On a journey without a scribe a pledge in hand (rihan maqbuda) is taken; A land deed made in a sealed copy and an open copy, witnessed and the silver weighed; A witness who hears a public adjuration and withholds testimony bears guilt; How many witnesses are required [divergence between the texts].

passages.text: כָּל מַ֨כֵּה נֶ֔פֶשׁ לְפִ֣י עֵדִ֔ים יִרְצַ֖ח אֶת הָרֹצֵ֑חַ וְעֵ֣ד אֶחָ֔ד לֹא יַעֲנֶ֥ה בְנֶ֖פֶשׁ לָמֽוּת

يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِذَا تَدَايَنتُم بِدَيْنٍ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى فَٱكْتُبُوهُ وَلْيَكْتُب بَّيْنَكُمْ كَاتِبٌۢ بِٱلْعَدْلِ وَلَا يَأْبَ كَاتِبٌ أَن يَكْتُبَ كَمَا عَلَّمَهُ ٱللَّهُ فَلْيَكْتُبْ وَلْيُمْلِلِ ٱلَّذِى عَلَيْهِ ٱلْحَقُّ وَلْيَتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ رَبَّهُۥ وَلَا يَبْخَسْ مِنْهُ شَيْـًٔا فَإِن كَانَ ٱلَّذِى عَلَيْهِ ٱلْحَقُّ سَفِيهًا أَوْ ضَعِيفًا أَوْ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُ أَن يُمِلَّ هُوَ فَلْيُمْلِلْ وَلِيُّهُۥ بِٱلْعَدْلِ وَٱسْتَشْهِدُوا۟ شَهِيدَيْنِ مِن رِّجَالِكُمْ فَإِن لَّمْ يَكُونَا رَجُلَيْنِ فَرَجُلٌ وَٱمْرَأَتَانِ مِمَّن تَرْضَوْنَ مِنَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءِ أَن تَضِلَّ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا ٱلْأُخْرَىٰ وَلَا يَأْبَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءُ إِذَا مَا دُعُوا۟ وَلَا تَسْـَٔمُوٓا۟ أَن تَكْتُبُوهُ صَغِيرًا أَوْ كَبِيرًا إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلِهِۦ ذَٰلِكُمْ أَقْسَطُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَأَقْوَمُ لِلشَّهَٰدَةِ وَأَدْنَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَرْتَابُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَ تِجَٰرَةً حَاضِرَةً تُدِيرُونَهَا بَيْنَكُمْ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَلَّا تَكْتُبُوهَا وَأَشْهِدُوٓا۟ إِذَا تَبَايَعْتُمْ وَلَا يُضَآرَّ كَاتِبٌ وَلَا شَهِيدٌ وَإِن تَفْعَلُوا۟ فَإِنَّهُۥ فُسُوقٌۢ بِكُمْ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمٌ

leads.title: The Nazirite vow ↔ New moons, fighting and the pilgrimage rites
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 1 deliberately changed, 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: When a consecrated person shaves the head [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The consecrated person lets his hair grow uncut as the sign of his vow (weight 6.7); One with an ailment of the head pays ransom by fasting, alms or sacrifice (weight 6.7). Pair score 20.1.

Only in The Nazirite vow: Priest places the boiled shoulder and cakes in the hands of the shaved Nazirite and waves them; Nazirite may not become unclean even for the corpse of father, mother, brother or sister; A man or a woman may take the vow of a Nazirite; Sudden death of someone beside a Nazirite voids his vow and he must start again; After the vow's completion rite the Nazirite may drink wine; Abstinence from wine, by vow or by general law [divergence between the texts]; Nazirite brings burnt, sin and well-being offerings with unleavened bread when his term ends; Nazirite abstains from wine, vinegar, grapes and everything from the vine down to seeds and skins; Nazirite's shaved hair is put on the fire under the well-being offering; Two turtledoves or two young pigeons offered (in place of a lamb if one cannot afford it).

Only in New moons, fighting and the pilgrimage rites: When you pour down from Arafat, remember God at the Sacred Monument (al-Mash'ar al-Haram); Take provision, but the best provision is God-consciousness (taqwa); Remember God on the counted days; no sin whether one hastens in two days or delays; Piety is not entering houses from their backs but from their doors; Fight in God's way those who fight you, but do not transgress; Prayer 'Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the next, and guard us from the fire'; Complete the pilgrimage (hajj) and visitation (umra) for God; Do not fight at the Sacred Mosque unless they fight you there; No sexual talk, wickedness or quarreling during the pilgrimage; Remember God as you remember your fathers, or more; The sacred month for the sacred month; violations are subject to retaliation; Do not shave heads until the sacrificial offering (hady) reaches its place; and 8 more.

matches.label: When a consecrated person shaves the head
matches.note: Num 6:5, 18 taʿar lōʾ yaʿăbōr ʿal rōʾšô ... wĕ-gillaḥ ha-nnāzîr petaḥ ʾōhel môʿēd ... wĕ-nātan ʿal hā-ʾēš ʾăšer taḥat zebaḥ ha-ššĕlāmîm: hair uncut during the vow, shaved at the sanctuary at its end and burned under the offering; Q 2:196 wa-lā taḥliqū ruʾūsakum ḥattā yablugha l-hadyu maḥillahu: no shaving in the pilgrim state until the offering reaches its place. The shaving tied to the offering is kept; the hair is not burned, and the rule applies to every pilgrim, not to a private vow.

passages.text: כָּל יְמֵי֙ נֶ֣דֶר נִזְר֔וֹ תַּ֖עַר לֹא יַעֲבֹ֣ר עַל רֹאשׁ֑וֹ עַד מְלֹ֨את הַיָּמִ֜ם אֲשֶׁר יַזִּ֤יר לַיהוָה֙ קָדֹ֣שׁ יִהְיֶ֔ה גַּדֵּ֥ל פֶּ֖רַע שְׂעַ֥ר רֹאשֽׁוֹ
וְגִלַּ֣ח הַנָּזִ֗יר פֶּ֛תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵ֖ד אֶת רֹ֣אשׁ נִזְר֑וֹ וְלָקַ֗ח אֶת שְׂעַר֙ רֹ֣אשׁ נִזְר֔וֹ וְנָתַן֙ עַל הָאֵ֔שׁ אֲשֶׁר תַּ֖חַת זֶ֥בַח הַשְּׁלָמִֽים

وَأَتِمُّوا۟ ٱلْحَجَّ وَٱلْعُمْرَةَ لِلَّهِ فَإِنْ أُحْصِرْتُمْ فَمَا ٱسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ ٱلْهَدْىِ وَلَا تَحْلِقُوا۟ رُءُوسَكُمْ حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ ٱلْهَدْىُ مَحِلَّهُۥ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوْ بِهِۦٓ أَذًى مِّن رَّأْسِهِۦ فَفِدْيَةٌ مِّن صِيَامٍ أَوْ صَدَقَةٍ أَوْ نُسُكٍ فَإِذَآ أَمِنتُمْ فَمَن تَمَتَّعَ بِٱلْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى ٱلْحَجِّ فَمَا ٱسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ ٱلْهَدْىِ فَمَن لَّمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَٰثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِى ٱلْحَجِّ وَسَبْعَةٍ إِذَا رَجَعْتُمْ تِلْكَ عَشَرَةٌ كَامِلَةٌ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن لَّمْ يَكُنْ أَهْلُهُۥ حَاضِرِى ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلْعِقَابِ

matches.label: One with an ailment of the head pays ransom by fasting, alms or sacrifice
matches.note: Num 6:9-10 wĕ-kî yāmût mēt ʿālāyw ... wĕ-gillaḥ rōʾšô ... yābiʾ šĕtê tōrîm ʾô šĕnê bĕnê yônâ: if the consecrated head is defiled he shaves early and brings an offering; Q 2:196 fa-man kāna minkum marīḍan aw bihi adhan min raʾsihi fa-fidyatun min ṣiyāmin aw ṣadaqatin aw nusuk: one forced to shave early because of a head ailment pays by fasting, alms or a sacrifice. Early shaving of a consecrated head, made good by an offering; the Quran gives three options.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Only in Father's appeal, the harlot as pit, and the drunkard's woes: Buy truth and do not sell it, wisdom, instruction and understanding; The drunkard is like one lying in the heart of the sea or on top of a mast; struck and feeling nothing, he seeks more on waking; Riddle-catalogue: 'Who has woe? who has sorrow? who has strife, wounds without cause, red eyes?' Only in Wine, gambling, orphans, mixed marriage and menstruation: A believing slave woman (or man) is better for marriage than an attractive polytheist; What to spend? Shared motifs, rarest first: God scorns the scorners but gives grace to the humble (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Proverbs 3:13-35, wisdom a tree of life; creation by wisdom; neighbor ethics: By God's knowledge the deeps were split open and the clouds drip dew; Do not withhold good from its owner or tell your neighbor 'Go and come back tomorrow' when you have it; The one who keeps wisdom lies down without fear; his sleep is sweet; he need not fear sudden terror; Wisdom 'is a tree of life to those who grasp her'; Wisdom holds length of days in her right hand, riches and honor in her left; Wisdom cannot be bought with gold of Ophir, onyx, sapphire, glass, coral, crystal, pearls or topaz of Cush; God made all his works in wisdom; Getting wisdom is better than gold, understanding than silver or jewels; Wisdom (hokhmah) personified as a woman who speaks in the first person.

leads.title: Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten) ↔ Call to worship the Creator; the challenge; paradise and the gnat
leads.summary: 3 correspondences read side by side: 1 deliberately changed, 1 same element, 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); God stretches out the heavens like a tent curtain (weight 6.3); God visits the earth with rain, softens it with showers, and crowns the year with harvest (weight 5.3). Pair score 18.3.

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; God makes the clouds his chariot and walks on the wings of the wind; All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n); God looks at the earth and it trembles, touches the mountains and they smoke; and 38 more.

Only in Call to worship the Creator; the challenge; paradise and the gnat: God is not ashamed to strike a parable of a gnat or something smaller; Fruits in paradise resemble those of earth: 'this is what we were given before'; A challenge to rivals to prove a divine claim [divergence between the texts]; The people break the covenant God made with them; Humans were dead, given life, will die and be given life again (two deaths, two lives); Hell's fire has men and stones as its fuel; The blessed have purified spouses (azwaj mutahhara) in paradise; God summons the coastlands and nations (and their gods) to a court trial to argue their case; God fashions seven heavens; Inimitability challenge: produce a surah like it, calling on your own witnesses (tahaddi); God opens his good storehouse, the heavens, to give rain; Paradise as gardens (of ʿAdn) beneath which rivers flow, where the righteous abide forever.

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; God makes the clouds his chariot and walks on the wings of the wind; All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n); God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; and 38 more.

leads.title: Psalm 105, historical hymn from the patriarchs through Joseph and the exodus ↔ Abraham, Ishmael and the House
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Only in Psalm 106, national confession of sins from Egypt to exile: Israel ate 'sacrifices of the dead' (zivhei metim) at Baal-peor; God caused the exiles to be pitied by all their captors; God grants the people's wilderness craving but sends wasting (razon) into their souls; Provoked at Meribah, Moses spoke rashly with his lips and suffered because of the people; Phinehas's intervention 'was reckoned to him as righteousness for all generations'; Israel 'yokes itself' to Baal of Peor; List of punishment types for the nations: stone-storm, the Shout, swallowing by the earth, drowning; The people exchanged their Glory for the image of an ox that eats grass; Moses 'stood in the breach' (pérets) before God to turn back his wrath from destroying the people; Speaker confesses personal sin and pleads for forgiveness and cleansing; God turned the sea into dry land and they crossed the river on foot; Shed blood pollutes the land and only the killer's blood atones for it; and 16 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: East and west belong to God; wherever you turn, there is the face of God (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Psalm 139, God's all-knowing presence and the embryo: Darkness is not dark to God; night shines like day, darkness and light are alike; 'YHWH, you have searched me and known me': God knows sitting and rising, thoughts from afar, every word before it is spoken; Nowhere to flee God's spirit: if I ascend to heaven you are there, if I make my bed in Sheol you are there; 'Do I not hate those who hate you, YHWH? I hate them with perfect hatred'; 'If I take the wings of the dawn (shahar) and dwell at the far end of the sea, even there your hand leads me'; No soul dies except by God's leave at a term written (kitaban mu'ajjalan); Speaker was made in secret and embroidered (ruqqamti) in the depths of the earth; No calamity befalls the earth or yourselves but it is in a Book before God brings it into being; Nothing wet or dry but is in a clear book; Fleeing from God, or to God [divergence between the texts]; God's knowledge of a person's thoughts and words, from afar or from near [divergence between the texts]; God knows what the earth diminishes of the dead bodies, and with him is a preserving record; and 15 more.

Only in Ra'ina, abrogation, rival claims and the face of God: Jews say the Christians stand on nothing, Christians say the same of the Jews; Claim that none enters paradise unless Jew or Christian, rebutted by surrender of the face to God; Believers told not to say 'ra'ina' (a word twisted by opponents) but 'unzurna'; God abrogates or causes to be forgotten a verse and brings a better or similar one (naskh); God swears by himself: to me every knee shall bow and every tongue swear; Whether God has or begets a son [contrast between the texts]; Whether God should speak to the people directly [contrast between the texts]; From sunrise to sunset God's name is great among the nations and in every place incense and a pure offering are brought to his name; 'He spoke and it came to be; he commanded and it stood firm'; Deity creates by spoken command (Let there be...); The called one asks for a sign that it is God who speaks [divergence between the texts]; The called one asks for a sign that it is God who speaks; and 2 more.

leads.title: Psalm 145, acrostic praise of the King (Ashrei) ↔ The fast of Ramadan
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: YHWH is near to all who call on him in truth (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Psalm 145, acrostic praise of the King (Ashrei): YHWH upholds all who fall and raises up all who are bowed down; An alphabetic acrostic lacks one letter of the alphabet; God's mercy encompasses all things; Praise (hamd) belongs to God, Lord of the worlds (rabb al-alamin); What the fathers told is to be passed on so that coming generations will tell their children; All creatures look to God to give their food in due season; he opens his hand and they are satisfied; All flesh, or all nations, come to God to pray or worship; God called al-Rahman and al-Rahim (the Merciful, the Compassionate), paired names from the root r-h-m (womb, mercy); 'Your kingdom is a kingdom of all ages and your dominion through all generations'; Formula of divine attributes: slow to anger, abundant in mercy, visits iniquity to fourth generation; The poem is an alphabetic acrostic (lines or stanzas begin with successive letters).

Only in The fast of Ramadan: Fasting prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you; Eat and drink until the white thread is distinguished from the black thread at dawn; Those able only with hardship may ransom fast days by feeding a poor person (fidya); Spouses not approached while in retreat (i'tikaf) in the mosques; Marital relations permitted on fast nights; spouses are garments for one another; Ramadan, the month in which the Quran was sent down; The sick and the traveler may make up missed fast days later; The wicked takes a bribe from the bosom to pervert the ways of justice; Marital relations during a fast [contrast between the texts]; What the annual fast is tied to [divergence between the texts]; Length, hours and exemptions of a prescribed fast [divergence between the texts]; 'These are the bounds (hudud) of God; do not approach (or transgress) them'; and 1 more.

leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Do not charge interest to the poor of my people (weight 5.8). Pair score 5.8.

Only in Psalm 15 - who may dwell on your holy mountain: The righteous keeps his oath even to his own hurt and does not change; The righteous does not slander with his tongue or take up reproach against his neighbor; Entrance liturgy: 'Who may dwell on your holy mountain?' answered by a list of ethical qualifications; God shows no partiality and takes no bribe; Psalm superscription ascribes the poem to David (le-david).

Only in Usury: God blots out usury and makes charity grow; A debtor in hardship is given respite until ease; remitting it as charity is better; Trade is like usury, they say; but God permitted trade and forbade usury (riba); Those who consume usury rise like one driven mad by Satan's touch; Those who do not give up usury are warned of war from God and his messenger; they keep their principal; Whether obligations differ toward insiders and outsiders [contrast between the texts]; Relief of debtors: release or respite [divergence between the texts]; To whom and how widely the ban on interest applies [divergence between the texts]; He who increases wealth by interest and usury gathers it for one who is gracious to the poor; Lending at interest or increase to a poor brother is forbidden.

leads.title: Psalm 19 - the heavens declare; the Torah is perfect ↔ Closing confession and prayer
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Prayer to be cleansed of hidden and unwitting faults (shegi'ot, nistarot) (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Psalm 19 - the heavens declare; the Torah is perfect: God has set a tent for the sun in the heavens; The Torah of YHWH is perfect, restoring the soul; its precepts make wise, gladden the heart, enlighten the eyes; 'May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before you, my Rock and Redeemer'; The heavens recount God's glory; day to day pours out speech without words or voice; The sun comes forth like a bridegroom from his chamber and rejoices like a strong man to run his course; God's judgments are more desirable than gold and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb; The seven heavens, the earth and everything in them glorify God, though humans do not understand their praise; Sun and moon each swim in an orbit (falak); God called the Rock (tsur); A solid firmament (raqia) separates upper waters from lower waters; Superscription 'for the leader/choirmaster' (lamenatseah).

Only in Closing confession and prayer: Prayer not to be laid with a burden (isr) like that laid on those before us; Believers make no distinction between any of the prophets (Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Tribes, Moses, Jesus); 'The soul that sins, it shall die': the son does not bear the father's iniquity nor the father the son's; 'We are the clay and you are our potter; we are all the work of your hand'; Believers' confession 'we hear and we obey' (sami'na wa-ata'na); God tests the hearts and the kidneys (inner self); God burdens no soul beyond its capacity; God alone knows the hearts of all humans.

leads.title: The final day on the Mount of Olives; living waters; Sukkot for the nations ↔ Abraham, Ishmael and the House
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 1 deliberately changed, 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: A sanctuary to which all peoples come [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Hear O Israel: YHWH our God, YHWH is one (weight 5.4). Pair score 12.1.

Only in The final day on the Mount of Olives; living waters; Sukkot for the nations: A unique day known to YHWH, neither day nor night, without light, cold and frost; at evening there will be light; The great earthquake in the days of King Uzziah is remembered as a reference point; Plague on Jerusalem's attackers: their flesh, eyes and tongues rot while they stand on their feet; In that day 'Holy to YHWH' is inscribed on the horses' bells and every pot in Jerusalem becomes holy; The whole land is leveled like the Arabah while Jerusalem is raised up on its site; Living waters flow out from Jerusalem, half to the eastern sea and half to the western sea, summer and winter; God's feet stand on the Mount of Olives, which splits east to west into a great valley, half moving north and half south; God gathers all nations to battle against Jerusalem: the city is taken, houses plundered, women raped, half exiled; Survivors of the nations go up yearly to Jerusalem to bow to the King, YHWH of hosts, and keep the feast of Booths; Families of the earth that do not go up for Sukkot get no rain; Egypt is struck with plague; There will no longer be a Canaanite (trader) in the house of YHWH; YHWH comes and all the holy ones (angels) with him; and 9 more.

Only in Abraham, Ishmael and the House: Abraham and Ishmael raise the foundations of the House while praying; Abraham told 'Submit' answers 'I submit to the Lord of the worlds' (aslamtu); God tests Abraham with words, he fulfills them and is made an imam for mankind; the covenant excludes the wrongdoers among his seed; The 'dye' or baptism (sibgha) of God: who has a better dye than God?; That was a community that has passed; it has what it earned and you what you earned; Dying Jacob asks his sons 'What will you worship after me?' and they confess the God of their fathers; Abraham and Ishmael pray that a messenger be raised from among their offspring; The chain of patriarchs to whom revelation or covenant passed [divergence between the texts]; Whether and how God's covenant with Abraham passes to his offspring [contrast between the texts]; The list of fathers in 'God of your fathers' [divergence between the texts]; Whether Ishmael is with Abraham or sent away [contrast between the texts]; Dying Jacob addresses his sons [divergence between the texts]; and 16 more.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness (weight 6.7); A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit (weight 6.0); First humans expelled from the garden (weight 6.0); God plants a garden (Eden) in the east and places the first human there (weight 5.6). Pair score 24.3.

Only in Adam, the angels and Iblis: The first man names the animals; God teaches Adam all the names and he recites them to the angels, who cannot; God commands the angels to prostrate before the first man, and they do; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; The expelled are told 'Go down, enemies to one another' with a dwelling and provision on earth for a time; The devil (Iblis) alone refuses to bow to the first man; God speaks in the plural (us, our) as if to a divine council; God announces to the angels he will place a vicegerent (khalifa) on earth; Formula 'no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve'; A tree of knowledge whose fruit is forbidden.

Only in Adam's forgetting, Iblis, the tree of immortality and the descent: God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve; God commands the angels to prostrate to Adam; all do except Iblis, who refuses; Satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans; Enmity between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed: head bruised, heel struck; Eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked; Fig leaves sewn into coverings; In the garden Adam will not hunger, be naked, thirst or suffer the sun's heat; Whoever turned from God's reminder is raised blind on judgment day: as he forgot the signs, so he is forgotten; The tempter offers 'the tree of immortality and a kingdom that never decays'; A tree whose fruit gives eternal life.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Forbidden: what has been consecrated (invoked over) to other than God (weight 6.7); Forbidden food is permitted to one compelled by necessity, without desire or transgression (weight 6.0); Eating blood is forbidden (weight 5.6); The pig is unclean and forbidden (weight 5.3). Pair score 23.6.

Only in Lawful food and true piety: Those who conceal scripture for gain eat only fire into their bellies; Eating an animal that died or was torn requires washing and makes unclean until evening; Refusal of revelation in favor of what was found with the fathers is rebuked; Wealth given for (freeing) necks, i.e. ransoming slaves and captives; Unbelievers are like beasts shouted at by a herdsman, hearing only a call and a cry; Piety (birr) is not turning faces east or west but faith, giving wealth to kin, orphans, poor, travelers, beggars and captives.

Only in Abrogation, the foreign teacher, coerced unbelief, food law, Abraham the hanif and the Sabbath (Surah 16:101-128): Abraham was a hanif, neither Jew nor Christian nor polytheist; God abrogates or causes to be forgotten a verse and brings a better or similar one (naskh); Opponents claim a foreign-tongued man teaches the prophet; answer: this is clear Arabic; Call to God's way with wisdom and good counsel and argue in the best way; One forced to disbelieve while his heart is firm in faith is excused; Only four foods are forbidden: carrion, blood, swine and what is offered to other than God; God sets a seal on the unbelievers' hearts and hearing and a covering over their eyes; Good foods once lawful were forbidden to the Jews as punishment for their wrongdoing; The Holy Spirit (ruh al-qudus) brings the revelation down from God; Follow the religion (milla) of Abraham the ḥanīf, who was no idolater; If you retaliate, do so in kind; but patience is better; The Sabbath was imposed only on those who differed about it; An opponent dismisses the revelation as inherited sorcery (sihr yu'thar) or 'only the word of a mortal'; Parable of a secure town supplied from everywhere which was ungrateful and was made to taste the garment of hunger and fear; Making some of God's provision unlawful and some lawful on your own authority is condemned.

leads.title: ʾamn: a security word concentrated in Abraham
leads.summary: أَمْن (ʾamn, “security”) occurs in 5 verses; 3 of them (60%) are in the Abraham narrative, which is 3% of the Quran, across 2 surahs. The more common same-gloss word مُؤْمِن (muʾmin, 193 verses) has only 3% of its verses there.

passages.text: وَإِذْ جَعَلْنَا ٱلْبَيْتَ مَثَابَةً لِّلنَّاسِ وَأَمْنًا وَٱتَّخِذُوا۟ مِن مَّقَامِ إِبْرَٰهِۦمَ مُصَلًّى وَعَهِدْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِۦمَ وَإِسْمَٰعِيلَ أَن طَهِّرَا بَيْتِىَ لِلطَّآئِفِينَ وَٱلْعَٰكِفِينَ وَٱلرُّكَّعِ ٱلسُّجُودِ

وَإِذَا جَآءَهُمْ أَمْرٌ مِّنَ ٱلْأَمْنِ أَوِ ٱلْخَوْفِ أَذَاعُوا۟ بِهِۦ وَلَوْ رَدُّوهُ إِلَى ٱلرَّسُولِ وَإِلَىٰٓ أُو۟لِى ٱلْأَمْرِ مِنْهُمْ لَعَلِمَهُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَسْتَنۢبِطُونَهُۥ مِنْهُمْ وَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُۥ لَٱتَّبَعْتُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا
وَكَيْفَ أَخَافُ مَآ أَشْرَكْتُمْ وَلَا تَخَافُونَ أَنَّكُمْ أَشْرَكْتُم بِٱللَّهِ مَا لَمْ يُنَزِّلْ بِهِۦ عَلَيْكُمْ سُلْطَٰنًا فَأَىُّ ٱلْفَرِيقَيْنِ أَحَقُّ بِٱلْأَمْنِ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَلَمْ يَلْبِسُوٓا۟ إِيمَٰنَهُم بِظُلْمٍ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمُ ٱلْأَمْنُ وَهُم مُّهْتَدُونَ

قُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ مِنْهَا جَمِيعًا فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ

وَإِذْ قُلْتُمْ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَن نَّصْبِرَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامٍ وَٰحِدٍ فَٱدْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُخْرِجْ لَنَا مِمَّا تُنۢبِتُ ٱلْأَرْضُ مِنۢ بَقْلِهَا وَقِثَّآئِهَا وَفُومِهَا وَعَدَسِهَا وَبَصَلِهَا قَالَ أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ ٱلَّذِى هُوَ أَدْنَىٰ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ خَيْرٌ ٱهْبِطُوا۟ مِصْرًا فَإِنَّ لَكُم مَّا سَأَلْتُمْ وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلذِّلَّةُ وَٱلْمَسْكَنَةُ وَبَآءُو بِغَضَبٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ يَكْفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ ٱلنَّبِيِّۦنَ بِغَيْرِ ٱلْحَقِّ ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَوا۟ وَّكَانُوا۟ يَعْتَدُونَ

ثُمَّ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُكُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَهِىَ كَٱلْحِجَارَةِ أَوْ أَشَدُّ قَسْوَةً وَإِنَّ مِنَ ٱلْحِجَارَةِ لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنْهُ ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَشَّقَّقُ فَيَخْرُجُ مِنْهُ ٱلْمَآءُ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَهْبِطُ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ
قَالَ فَٱهْبِطْ مِنْهَا فَمَا يَكُونُ لَكَ أَن تَتَكَبَّرَ فِيهَا فَٱخْرُجْ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰغِرِينَ

passages.text: وَإِذْ وَٰعَدْنَا مُوسَىٰٓ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً ثُمَّ ٱتَّخَذْتُمُ ٱلْعِجْلَ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ وَأَنتُمْ ظَٰلِمُونَ

وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا عَرَّضْتُم بِهِۦ مِنْ خِطْبَةِ ٱلنِّسَآءِ أَوْ أَكْنَنتُمْ فِىٓ أَنفُسِكُمْ عَلِمَ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ سَتَذْكُرُونَهُنَّ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تُوَاعِدُوهُنَّ سِرًّا إِلَّآ أَن تَقُولُوا۟ قَوْلًا مَّعْرُوفًا وَلَا تَعْزِمُوا۟ عُقْدَةَ ٱلنِّكَاحِ حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ ٱلْكِتَٰبُ أَجَلَهُۥ وَٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِىٓ أَنفُسِكُمْ فَٱحْذَرُوهُ وَٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ

وَوَٰعَدْنَا مُوسَىٰ ثَلَٰثِينَ لَيْلَةً وَأَتْمَمْنَٰهَا بِعَشْرٍ فَتَمَّ مِيقَٰتُ رَبِّهِۦٓ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِأَخِيهِ هَٰرُونَ ٱخْلُفْنِى فِى قَوْمِى وَأَصْلِحْ وَلَا تَتَّبِعْ سَبِيلَ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ
يَٰبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ قَدْ أَنجَيْنَٰكُم مِّنْ عَدُوِّكُمْ وَوَٰعَدْنَٰكُمْ جَانِبَ ٱلطُّورِ ٱلْأَيْمَنَ وَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلْوَىٰ

leads.title: yastaḥāi: a live word concentrated in Moses
leads.summary: يَسْتَحْىِۦ (yastaḥāi, “live”) occurs in 8 verses; 5 of them (62%) are in the Moses narrative, which is 7% of the Quran, across 4 surahs. The more common same-gloss word سَكَنَ (sakana, 15 verses) has only 13% of its verses there.

lexical.gloss: to live, whether literally or figuratively (H2421, possible cognate)

passages.text: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَسْتَحْىِۦٓ أَن يَضْرِبَ مَثَلًا مَّا بَعُوضَةً فَمَا فَوْقَهَا فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ فَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ ٱلْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمْ وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ فَيَقُولُونَ مَاذَآ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَٰذَا مَثَلًا يُضِلُّ بِهِۦ كَثِيرًا وَيَهْدِى بِهِۦ كَثِيرًا وَمَا يُضِلُّ بِهِۦٓ إِلَّا ٱلْفَٰسِقِينَ
وَإِذْ نَجَّيْنَٰكُم مِّنْ ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوٓءَ ٱلْعَذَابِ يُذَبِّحُونَ أَبْنَآءَكُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِسَآءَكُمْ وَفِى ذَٰلِكُم بَلَآءٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ

وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَأُ مِن قَوْمِ فِرْعَوْنَ أَتَذَرُ مُوسَىٰ وَقَوْمَهُۥ لِيُفْسِدُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَيَذَرَكَ وَءَالِهَتَكَ قَالَ سَنُقَتِّلُ أَبْنَآءَهُمْ وَنَسْتَحْىِۦ نِسَآءَهُمْ وَإِنَّا فَوْقَهُمْ قَٰهِرُونَ
وَإِذْ أَنجَيْنَٰكُم مِّنْ ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوٓءَ ٱلْعَذَابِ يُقَتِّلُونَ أَبْنَآءَكُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِسَآءَكُمْ وَفِى ذَٰلِكُم بَلَآءٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ

وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِ ٱذْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَةَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ أَنجَىٰكُم مِّنْ ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوٓءَ ٱلْعَذَابِ وَيُذَبِّحُونَ أَبْنَآءَكُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِسَآءَكُمْ وَفِى ذَٰلِكُم بَلَآءٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ
إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ عَلَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَجَعَلَ أَهْلَهَا شِيَعًا يَسْتَضْعِفُ طَآئِفَةً مِّنْهُمْ يُذَبِّحُ أَبْنَآءَهُمْ وَيَسْتَحْىِۦ نِسَآءَهُمْ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ

يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تَدْخُلُوا۟ بُيُوتَ ٱلنَّبِىِّ إِلَّآ أَن يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ إِلَىٰ طَعَامٍ غَيْرَ نَٰظِرِينَ إِنَىٰهُ وَلَٰكِنْ إِذَا دُعِيتُمْ فَٱدْخُلُوا۟ فَإِذَا طَعِمْتُمْ فَٱنتَشِرُوا۟ وَلَا مُسْتَـْٔنِسِينَ لِحَدِيثٍ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكُمْ كَانَ يُؤْذِى ٱلنَّبِىَّ فَيَسْتَحْىِۦ مِنكُمْ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَسْتَحْىِۦ مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ وَإِذَا سَأَلْتُمُوهُنَّ مَتَٰعًا فَسْـَٔلُوهُنَّ مِن وَرَآءِ حِجَابٍ ذَٰلِكُمْ أَطْهَرُ لِقُلُوبِكُمْ وَقُلُوبِهِنَّ وَمَا كَانَ لَكُمْ أَن تُؤْذُوا۟ رَسُولَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَآ أَن تَنكِحُوٓا۟ أَزْوَٰجَهُۥ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦٓ أَبَدًا إِنَّ ذَٰلِكُمْ كَانَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ عَظِيمًا
فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُم بِٱلْحَقِّ مِنْ عِندِنَا قَالُوا۟ ٱقْتُلُوٓا۟ أَبْنَآءَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مَعَهُۥ وَٱسْتَحْيُوا۟ نِسَآءَهُمْ وَمَا كَيْدُ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍ

leads.title: Who are the Quran's Sabians?
leads.summary: The Quran names the Sabians (al-Ṣābiʾūn) beside Jews and Christians. Candidates include the Mandaeans, the pagans of Harran, and Elchasaite baptists.

passages.text: (2:62) إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ وَٱلصَّٰبِـِٔينَ مَنْ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًا فَلَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ (5:69) إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ وَٱلصَّٰبِـُٔونَ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ مَنْ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًا فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ (22:17) إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ وَٱلصَّٰبِـِٔينَ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ وَٱلْمَجُوسَ وَٱلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوٓا۟ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ شَهِيدٌ

evidence.text: A proposed etymology links the name to Aramaic/Mandaic ṣbaʿ 'immerse', which would fit a baptist group.
